title: A Child of The King (My Father is Rich in Houses and Lands)
author: Harriet Eugenia Peck Buell

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: My Father is rich in houses and lands,
He holdeth the wealth of the world in His hands!
Of rubies and diamonds of silver and gold His coffers are full,He has riches untold.
I'm a child of the King, a child of the King:

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: My Father's own Son, the Savior of men,
Once wander'd o'er earth as the poorest of men,
But now He is reigning forever on high,
And will give me a home in heaven by and by.
With Jesus my Savior I'm a child of the King.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: I once was an outcast stranger on earth,
A sinner by choice, and an alien by birth!
But I've been adopted, my name's written down,An heir to a mansion, a robe, and a crown.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: A tent or a cottage, why should I care?
They're building a palace for me over there!
Tho' exiled from home, yet, still I may sing: All glory to God,
I'm the child of a King.

title: A Great and Mighty Wonder
author: Germanus of Constantinople

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: A great and mighty wonder, a full and holy cure: The virgin bears the Infant with virgin honor pure!

blocks.label: Refrain
lines: Repeat the hymn again: "To God on high be glory And peace on earth to men!"

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: The Word becomes incarnate and yet remains on high,
And cherubim sing anthems to shepherds from the sky.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: While thus they sing your Monarch, those bright angelic bands,
Rejoice, ye vales and mountains, ye oceans, clap your hands.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Since all He comes to ransom, by all be He adored,
The Infant born in Bethl'em, the Savior and the Lord.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: And idol forms shall perish, and error shall decay,
And Christ shall wield His scepter, our Lord and God for aye.

title: A Lamb Goes Uncomplaining Forth
author: Paul Gerhardt

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: A Lamb goes uncomplaining forth,
The guilt of all men bearing;
And laden with the sins of earth,
None else the burden sharing!
Goes patient on, grow weak and faint,
To slaughter led with out complaint,
That spotless life to offer;
Bears shame and stripes, and wounds and death,
Anguish and mocker y, and saith, "Willing all this I suf* fer."

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: This Lamb is Christ, the soul's great Friend,
The Lamb of God, our Savior;
Him God the Father chose to send To gain for us His favor.
"Go forth,
My Son," the Father saith, "And free men from the fear of death,
From guilt and condemnation.
The wrath and stripes are hard to bear,
But by Thy Passion men shall share The fruit of Thy salva* tion."

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: "Yea,
Father, yea, most willingly I'll bear what Thou com* mandest;
My will conforms to Thy decree,
I do what Thou de* mandest." O wondrous Love, what hast Thou done!
The Father offers up His Son!
The Son, content, descendeth!
O Love, how strong Thou art to save!
Thou beddest Him with in the grave Whose word the mountains ren* deth.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Thou lay'st Him,
Love, upon the cross,
With nails and spear Him bruising;
Thou slay'st Him as a lamb,
His loss from soul and body oozing;
From body 'tis the crimson flood Of precious sacri ficial blood From soul, the strength of anguish: My gain it is;
sweet Lamb to Thee What can I give, whose love to me For me doth make Thee lan* guish?

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Lord, all my life I'll cleave to Thee,
Thy love fore'er be* holding,
Thee ever, as Thou ever me,
With loving arms en* folding.
Yea,
Thou shalt be my Beaconlight,
To guide me safe through death's dark night.
And cheer my heart in sorrow;
Henceforth my self and all that's mine To Thee, my Savior,
I consign,
From whom all things I bor* row.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: From morn till eve my theme shall be
Thy mercy's wondrous measure;
To sacrifice myself for Thee
Shall be my aim and pleasure.
My stream of life shall ever be
A current flowing ceaselessly,
Thy constant praise outpouring.
I'll treasure in my memory,
O Lord, all Thou hast done for me,
Thy gracious love adoring.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: Enlarge, my heart's own shrine, and swell,
To thee shall now be given
A treasure that doth far excel
The worth of earth and heaven.
Away with the Arabian gold,
With treasures of an earthly mold!
I've found a better jewel.
My priceless treasure, Lord my God,
Is Thy most holy, precious blood,
Which flowed from wounds so cruel.

blocks.label: Verse 8
lines: This treasure ever I'll employ,
This every aid shall yield me;
In sorrow it shall be my joy,
In conflict it shall shield me;
In joy, the music of my feast,
And when all else has lost its zest,
This manna still shall feed me;
In thirst my drink; in want my food;
My company in solitude,
To comfort and to lead me.

blocks.label: Verse 9
lines: Of death I am no more afraid,
New life from Thee is flowing;
Thy cross affords me cooling shade
When noonday's sun is glowing.
When by my grief I am oppressed,
On Thee my weary soul shall rest
Serenely as on pillows.
Thou art my Anchor when by woe
My bark is driven to and fro
On trouble's surging billows.

blocks.label: Verse 10
lines: And when Thy glory I shall see
And taste Thy kingdom's pleasure,
Thy blood my royal robe shall be,
My joy beyond all measure.
When I appear before Thy throne,
Thy righteousness shall be my crown-
With these I need not hide me.
And there, in garments richly wrought
As Thine own bride, I shall be brought
To stand in joy beside Thee.

title: A Mighty Fortress Is Our God
author: Martin Luther

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: A mighty for* tress is our God, a bulwark never fail* ing;
Our helper He, amid the flood of mortal ills prevail* ing: For still our ancient foe doth seek to work us woe;
His craft and pow'r are great, and, armed with cruel hate,
On earth is not his e* qual.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Did we in our own strength confide, our striving would be lo* sing;
Were not the right Man on our side, the Man of God's own choos* ing: Dost ask who that may be?
Christ Jesus, it is He;
Lord Sabaoth,
His name, from age to age the same,
And He must win the bat* tle.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: And though this world, with dev* ils filled, should threaten to undo us,
We will not fear, for God hath willed His truth to triumph through us: The Prince of Darkness grim, we tremble not for him;
His rage we can endure, for lo, his doom is sure,
One little word shall fell him.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: That word above all earth* ly pow'rs, no thanks to them, abid* eth;
The Spirit and the gifts are ours through Him who with us si* deth: Let goods and kindred go, this mortal life also;
The body they may kill: God's truth abideth still,
His kingdom is forev* er.

title: Abide, O Dearest Jesus
author: Joshua Stegmann

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Abide,
O dearest Jesus,
Among us with Thy grace,
That Satan may not harm us,
Nor we to sin give place.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Abide,
O dear Redeemer,
Among us with Thy Word,
And thus now and hereafter True peace and joy afford.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Abide with heav'nly brightness Among us, precious Light;
Thy truth direct, and keep us From error's gloomy night.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Abide with richest blessings Among us, bounteous Lord;
Let us in grace and wisdom Grow daily through Thy Word.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Abide with Thy protection Among us,
Lord, our Strength,
Lest world and Satan fell us And overcome at length.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: Abide, O faithful Savior, Among us with Thy love;
Grant steadfastness, and help us To reach our home above.

title: Abide With Me
author: Henry F. Lyte

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Abide with me;
fast falls the eventide;
The darkness deepens;
Lord with me abide.
When other helpers fail and comforts flee,
Help of the helpless,
O abide with me.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Swift to its close ebbs out life's little day;
Earth's joys grow dim;
its glories pass away;
Change and decay in all around I see;
O Thou who changest not, abide with me.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Not a brief glance I beg, a passing word;
But as Thou dwell'st with Thy disciples,
Lord,
Familiar, condes cending, patient, free.
Come not to sojourn, but abide with me.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Come not in terrors, as the King of kings,
But kind and good, with healing in Thy wings,
Tears for all woes, a heart for every plea?
Come,
Friend of sinners, and thus bide with me.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Thou on my head in early youth didst smile;
And, though re bellious and perverse meanwhile,
Thou hast not left me, oft as I left Thee,
On to the close,
O Lord, abide with me.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: I need Thy presence every passing hour.
What but Thy grace can foil the tempter's power?
Who, like Thyself, my guide and stay can be?
Through cloud and sunshine, Lord, abide with me.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: I fear no foe, with Thee at hand to bless;
Ills have no weight, and tears no bitterness.
Where is death's sting? Where, grave, thy victory?
I triumph still, if Thou abide with me.

blocks.label: Verse 8
lines: Hold Thou Thy cross before my closing eyes;
Shine through the gloom and point me to the skies.
Heaven's morning breaks, and earth's vain shadows flee;
In life, in death, O Lord, abide with me.

title: All Creatures of Our God and King
author: Francis of Assisi

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: All creatures of our God and King Lift up your voice and with us sing,
Alleluia!
Alleluia!
Thou burning sun with golden beam,
Thou silver moon with softer gleam!
O praise Him!

blocks.label: Refrain
lines: O praise Him!
Alleluia!
Alleluia!
Alleluia!

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Thou rushing wind that art so strong Ye clouds that sail in Heaven along,
O praise Him!
Alleluia!
Thou rising moon, in praise rejoice,
Ye lights of evening, find a voice!

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Thou flowing water, pure and clear,
Make music for thy Lord to hear,
O praise Him!
Alleluia!
Thou fire so masterful and bright,
That givest man both warmth and light.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Dear mother earth, who day by day Unfoldest blessings on our way,
O praise Him!
Alleluia!
The flowers and fruits that in thee grow,
Let them His glory also show.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: And all ye men of tender heart,
Forgiving others, take your part,
O sing ye!
Alleluia!
Ye who long pain and sorrow bear,
Praise God and on Him cast your care!

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: And thou most kind and gentle Death,
Waiting to hush our latest breath,
O praise Him! Alleluia!
Thou leadest home the child of God,
And Christ our Lord the way hath trod.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: Let all things their Creator bless,
And worship Him in humbleness,
O praise Him! Alleluia!
Praise, praise the Father, praise the Son,
And praise the Spirit, Three in One!

title: All Depends On Our Possessing
author: unknown

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: All depends on our possessing God's abundant grace and blessing,
Though all earthly wealth depart.
He who trusts with faith unshaken In His God is not forsaken And e'er keeps a dauntless heart.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: He who hitherto hath fed me And to many joys hath led me,
Is and ever shall be mine.
He who did so gently school me,
He who still doth guide and rule me,
Will remain my Help divine.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Many spend their lives in fretting Over trifles and in getting Things that have no solid ground.
I shall strive to win a treasure That will bring me lasting pleasure And that now is seldom found.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: When with sorrow I am stricken,
Hope my heart anew will quicken,
All my longing shall be stilled.
To His lovingkindness tender Soul and body I surrender;
For in Him alone I build.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Well He knows what best to grant me;
All the longing hopes that haunt me,
Joy and sorrow, have their day.
I shall doubt His wisdom never,
As God wills, so be it ever,
I to Him commit my way.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: If on earth my days He lengthen,
He my weary soul will strengthen;
All my trust in Him I place.
Earthly wealth is not abiding,
Like a stream away is gliding;
Safe I anchor in His grace.

title: All Hail The Power Of Jesus' Name
author: Edward Perronet

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: All hail the pow'r of Jesus' Name!
Let angels prostrate fall;
Bring forth the royal di* a* dem, and crown Him Lord of all.
Bring forth the royal di* a* dem, and crown Him Lord of all.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Let highborn seraphs tune the lyre, and as they tune it, fall Before His face Who tunes their choir, and crown Him Lord of all.
Before His face Who tunes their choir, and crown Him Lord of all.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Crown Him, ye morning stars of light, who fixed this floating ball;
Now hail the strength of Is* rael's might, and crown Him Lord of all.
Now hail the strength of Is* rael's might, and crown Him Lord of all.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Crown Him, ye martyrs of your God, who from His altar call;
Extol the Stem of Je* sse's Rod, and crown Him Lord of all.
Extol the Stem of Je* sse's Rod, and crown Him Lord of all.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Ye seed of Israel's chosen race, ye ransomed from the fall,
Hail Him Who saves you by His grace, and crown Him Lord of all.
Hail Him Who saves you by His grace, and crown Him Lord of all.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: Hail Him, ye heirs of David's line, whom David Lord did call,
The God incarnate, Man divine, and crown Him Lord of all,
The God incarnate, Man divine, and crown Him Lord of all.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: Sinners, whose love can ne'er forget the wormwood and the gall,
Go spread your trophies at His feet, and crown Him Lord of all.
Go spread your trophies at His feet, and crown Him Lord of all.

blocks.label: Verse 8
lines: Let every tribe and every tongue before Him prostrate fall
And shout in universal song the crown�d Lord of all.
And shout in universal song the crown�d Lord of all.

title: All My Heart This Night Rejoices (All My Heart Again Rejoices)
author: Paul Gerhardt

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: All my heart this night rejoices,
As I hear,
Far and near,
Sweetest angel voices;
"Christ is born," their choirs are singing,
Till the air Ev'rywhere Now with joy is ringing.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: For it dawns,the promised morrow Of His birth Who the earth Rescues from her sorrow.
God to wear our form de scendeth,
Of His grace To our race Here His Son He lendeth:

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Yea, so truly for us careth,
That His Son All we've done As our off'ring beareth;
As our Lamb who, dying for us,
Bears our load,
And to God Doth in peace restore us.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Hark!
a voice from yonder manger,
Soft and sweet,
Doth entreat, "Flee from woe and danger;
Brethren come, from all doth grieve you You are freed,
All you need I will surely give you."

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Come then, let us hasten yonder;
Here let all,
Great and small,
Kneel in awe and wonder.
Love Him who with love is yearning;
Hail the Star That from far Bright with hope is burning!

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: Ye who pine in weary sadness, Weep no more, For the door
Now is found of gladness. Cling to Him for He will guide you
Where no cross, Pain or loss, Can again betide you.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: Hither come, ye heavy\- hearted, Who for sin Deep within,
Long and sore have smarted; For the poison'd wounds you're feeling
Help is near, One is here Mighty for their healing!

blocks.label: Verse 8
lines: Hither come, ye poor and wretched; Know His will Is to fill
Every hand outstretched; Here are riches without measure,
Here forget All regret, Fill your hearts with treasure.

blocks.label: Verse 9
lines: Blessed Savior, let me find Thee! Keep Thou me Close to Thee,
Cast me not behind Thee! Life of life, my heart Thou stillest,
Calm I rest On Thy breast, All this void Thou fillest.

blocks.label: Verse 10
lines: Thee, dear Lord, with heed I'll cherish, Live to Thee, And with Thee
Dying, shall not perish; But shall dwell with Thee for ever,
Far on high In the joy That can alter never.

title: All Praise To Thee, My God, This Night
author: Thomas Ken

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: All praise to Thee, my God, this night,
For all the blessings of the light!
Keep me,
O keep me,
King of kings,
Beneath Thine own almighty wings.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Forgive me,
Lord, for Thy dear Son,
The ill that I this day have done,
That with the world, myself, and Thee,
I, ere I sleep, at peace may be.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Teach me to live, that I may dread The grave as little as my bed.
Teach me to die, that so I may Rise glorious at the judgment day.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: O may my soul on Thee repose,
And with sweet sleep mine eyelids close,
Sleep that may me more vig'rous make To serve my God when I awake.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: When in the night I sleepless lie,
My soul with heav'nly thoughts supply;
Let no ill dreams disturb my rest,
No pow'rs of darkness me molest.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: O when shall I, in endless day,
For ever chase dark sleep away,
And hymns divine with angels sing,
All praise to thee, eternal King?

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: Praise God, from Whom all blessings flow;
Praise Him, all creatures here below;
Praise Him above, ye heavenly host;
Praise Father, Son, and Holy Ghost.

title: All Praise to Jesus' Hallowed Name
author: Martin German;Luther

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: All praise to Jesus' hallowed Name Who of virgin pure became True man for us!
The angels sing As the glad news to earth they bring.
Hallelujah!

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Th'Eternal Father's only Son For a manger leaves His throne Disguised in our poor flesh and blood See now the everlasting Good.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: He whom the world could not inwrap Yonder lies in Mary's lap;
He is become an infant small,
Who by His might upholdeth all.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Th'Eternal Light, come down from heav'n,
Hath to us new sunshine giv'n;
It shineth in the midst of night,
And maketh us the sons of light.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: The Father's Son,
God everblest,
In the world be came a guest;
He leads us from this vale of tears,
And makes us in his kingdom heirs.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: He came to earth so mean and poor, Man to pity and restore,
And make us rich in heaven above, Equal with angels through his love.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: All this He did to show His grace To our poor and sinful race;
For this let Christendom adore And praise His name for evermore.

title: All Who Believe and Are Baptized (He That Believes and Is Baptized)
author: Thomas Hansen Kingo

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: All who believe and are baptized shall see the Lord's salva* tion;
baptized into the death of Christ, they are a new crea* tion.
through Christ's redemption they shall stand among the glorious heav'nly band of every tribe and na* tion.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: With one accord,
O God, we pray: grant us thy Holy Spi* rit;
look thou on our infirmity through Jesus' blood and mer* it.
Grant us to grow in grace each day that by this sacra ment we may eternal life inher* it.

title: Alleluia, Alleluia! Hearts to Heaven and Voices Raise
author: Christopher Wordsworth

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Alleluia, alleluia!
Hearts to Heav'n and voices raise: Sing to God a hymn of gladness, sing to God a hymn of praise.
He, who on the cross a Victim, for the world's salvation bled,
Jesus Christ, the King of glory, now is risen from the dead.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Now the iron bars are broken,
Christ from death to life is born,
Glorious life, and life immortal, on the holy Easter morn.
Christ has triumphed, and we conquer by His mighty enterprise: We with Him to life eternal by His resurrection rise.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Christ is risen,
Christ, the first fruits of the holy harvest field,
Which will all its full abundance at His second coming yield: Then the golden ears of harvest will their heads before Him wave,
Ripened by His glorious sunshine from the furrows of the grave.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Christ is risen, we are risen!
Shed upon us heav'nly grace,
Rain and dew and gleams of glory from the brightness of Thy face;
That we, with our hearts in Heaven, here on earth may fruitful be,
And by angel hands be gathered, and be ever,
Lord, with Thee.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Alleluia, alleluia!
Glory be to God on high;
Alleluia!
to the Savior who has gained the victory;
Alleluia!
to the Spirit, fount of love and sanctity: Alleluia, alleluia!
to the Triune Majesty.

title: Alleluia, Sing To Jesus!
author: William Chatterton Dix

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Allelu* ia!
sing to Je* sus!
His the scepter,
His the throne.
Allelu* ia!
His the tri* umph,
His the victory alone.
Hark!
the songs of peaceful Zi* on thunder like a might* y flood.
Je* sus out of ev* ery na* tion has redeemed us by His blood.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Allelu* ia!
not as or* phans are we left in sor* row now;
Allelu* ia!
He is near us, faith believes, nor ques* tions how;
Though the cloud from sight received Him when the for* ty days were o'er Shall our hearts forget His pro* mise, "I am with you evermore"?

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Allelu* ia!
bread of an* gels,
Thou on earth our food, our stay;
Allelu* ia!
here the sin* ful flee to Thee from day to day: Interces* sor,
Friend of sin* ners,
Earth's Redeem* er, plead for me,
Where the songs of all the sin* less sweep across the crystal sea.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Allelu* ia!
King eter* nal,
Thee the Lord of lords we own;
Allelu* ia!
born of Mar* y,
Earth Thy footstool,
Heaven Thy throne: Thou within the veil hast en* tered, robed in flesh our great High Priest;
Thou on earth both priest and vic* tim in the Eu* charistic feast.

title: Almighty God Your Word Is Cast
author: John Cawood

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Almighty God,
Your Word is cast Like seed into the ground;
Now let the dew of Heav'n descend,
And righteous fruits abound.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Let not the foe of Christ and man This holy seed remove,
But give it root in ev'ry heart To bring forth fruits of love.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Let not the world's deceitful cares The rising plant destroy.
But let it yield a hundredfold The fruits of peace and joy.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Nor let Your Word so kindly sent To raise us to Your throne Return to You, and sadly tell That we reject Your Son.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Oft as the precious seed is sown,
Your quick'ning grace bestow,
That all whose souls the truth receive,
Its saving power may know.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: Great God, come down and on Your Word
Your mighty power bestow,
That all who hear the joyful sound,
Your saving grace may know.

title: Amazing Grace
author: John Newton

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Amazing grace!
How sweet the sound That saved a wretch like me!
I once was lost, but now am found;
Was blind, but now I see.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: 'Twas grace that taught my heart to fear,
And grace my fears relieved;
How pre* cious did that grace ap* pear The hour I first believed.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Through many dangers, toils and snares,
I have al* ready come;
'Tis grace hath brought me safe thus far,
And grace will lead me home.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: The Lord has promised good to me,
His Word my hope secures;
He will my Shield and Por* tion be,
As long as life endures.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Yea, when this flesh and heart shall fail,
And mortal life shall cease,
I shall pos* sess, with in the veil,
A life of joy and peace.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: The earth shall soon dissolve like snow,
The sun forbear to shine;
But God, Who called me here below,
Shall be forever mine.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: When we've been there ten thousand years,
Bright shining as the sun,
We've no less days to sing God's praise
Than when we'd first begun.

title: And Can It Be
author: Charles Wesley

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: And can it be that I should gain An interest in the Savior's blood?
Died He for me, who caused His pain?
For me, who Him to death pursued?
Ama* zing love!
How can it be,
That Thou, my God, shouldst die for me?

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: 'Tis mys* tery all: th'Immortal dies: Who can explore His strange design?
In vain the first* born seraph tries To sound the depths of love divine.
'Tis mer* cy all!
Let earth adore,
Let angel minds inquire no more.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: He left His Father's throne above So free, so in* fi nite His grace?
Emptied Himself of all but love,
And bled for A* dam's helpless race: 'Tis mer* cy all, immense and free,
For O my God, it found out me!

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Long my imprisoned spirit lay,
Fast bound in sin and nature's night;
Thine eye diffused a quick'ning ray?
I woke, the dun* geon flamed with light;
My chains fell off, my heart was free,
I rose, went forth, and followed Thee.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Still the small inward voice I hear,
That whispers all my sins forgiv'n;
Still the aton* ing blood is near,
That quenched the wrath of hostile Heav'n.
I feel the life His wounds impart;
I feel the Sa* vior in my heart.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: No condemnation now I dread; Jesus, and all in Him, is mine;
Alive in Him, my living Head, And clothed in righteousness divine,
Bold I approach th'eternal throne, And claim the crown, through Christ my own.

title: Angel Voices, Ever Singing
author: Francis Pott

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Angel voices, ever singing, round Thy throne of light,
Angel harps, forever ringing, rest not day or night;
Thousands only live to bless Thee, and confess Thee Lord of might.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Thou Who art beyond the farthest mortal eye can scan,
Can it be that Thou regardest songs of sinful man?
Can we feel that Thou art near us and wilt hear us?
Yea, we can.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Lord, we know Thy love rejoices o'er each work of Thine;
Thou didst ears and hands and voices for Thy praise combine;
Craftsman's art and music's measure for Thy pleasure didst design.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Here, great God, today we offer of Thine own to Thee;
And for Thine acceptance proffer, all unworthily,
Hearts and minds, and hands and voices, in our choicest melody.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Honor, glory, might and merit,
Thine shall ever be,
Father,
Son, and Holy Spirit, blessed Trinity;
Of the best that Thou hast given Earth and Heaven render Thee.

title: Angels From the Realms of Glory
author: James Montgomery

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Angels from the realms of glory,
Wing your flight o'er all the earth;
Ye who sang creation's story Now proclaim Mes* siah's birth.

blocks.label: Refrain
lines: Come and worship, come and worship,
Worship Christ, the newborn King.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Shepherds, in the field abiding,
Watching o'er your flocks by night,
God with us is now residing;
Yonder shines the infant light:

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Sages, leave your contemplations,
Brighter visions beam afar;
Seek the great Desire of nations;
Ye have seen His natal star.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Saints, before the altar bending,
Watching long in hope and fear;
Suddenly the Lord, descending,
In His temple shall appear.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Sinners, wrung with true repentance,
Doomed for guilt to endless pains,
Justice now revokes the sentence,
Mercy calls you;
break your chains.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: Though an Infant now we view Him,
He shall fill His Father's throne,
Gather all the nations to Him;
Every knee shall then bow down:

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: All creation, join in praising
God, the Father, Spirit, Son,
Evermore your voices raising
To th'eternal Three in One.

title: Angels We Have Heard On High
author: French

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Angels we have heard on high Sweetly singing o'er the plains,
And the mountains in reply Echoing their joyous strains.
Glo* ria, in excelsis Deo!

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Shepherds, why this jubilee?
Why your joyous strains prolong?
What the gladsome tidings be Which inspire your heav'nly song?
Glo* ria, in excelsis De* o!

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Come to Bethlehem and see Christ Whose birth the angels sing;
Come, adore on bended knee,
Christ the Lord, the newborn King.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: See Him in a manger laid,
Whom the choirs of angels praise;
Mary,
Joseph, lend your aid,
While our hearts in love we raise.

title: As With Gladness Men of Old
author: William Chatterton Dix

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: As with gladness, men of old Did the guiding star behold As with joy they hailed its light Leading onward, beaming bright So, most glorious Lord, may we Evermore be led to Thee.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: As with joyful steps they sped To that lowly manger bed There to bend the knee before Him whom Heav'n and earth adore;
So may we with willing feet Ever seek Thy mercy seat.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: As they offered gifts most rare At that manger rude and bare;
So may we with holy joy,
Pure and free from sin's alloy,
All our costliest treasures bring,
Christ, to Thee, our heav'nly King.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Holy Jesus, ev'ry day Keep us in the narrow way;
And, when earthly things are past,
Bring our ransomed souls at last Where they need no star to guide,
Where no clouds Thy glory hide.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: In the heav'nly country bright,
Need they no created light;
Thou its Light, its Joy, its Crown,
Thou its Sun which goes not down;
There forever may we sing Alleluias to our King!

title: Ascribe To the Lord Honor
author: 'Bola Omodun. Ilori

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Ascribe to the Lord, honor,
And glory due His Name Worship in His holiness,
Worthy is His pow'r and fame.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: The Lord of glory thunders O'er great and mighty seas;
His voice is so majestic,
It breaks cedar to pieces.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: His voice like a mighty flash,
Shakes the desert of Kadesh,
It makes bare the thick forest No other voice is its match.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: The Lord sits upon His throne,
That's set upon the flood.
He gives strength to His people,
Who put their trust in His word.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Ascribe to the Lord, honor,
And glory due His Name,
Worship Him in holiness Worthy is His might and fame.

title: At The Lamb's High Feast
author: Latin

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: At the Lamb's high feast we sing,
Praise to our victor* ious King,
Who has washed us in the tide Flowing from his pierc�d side;
Alleluia!

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Praise we Him, whose love divine Gives His sacred blood for wine,
Gives His body for the feast,
Christ the Victim,
Christ the Priest.
Alleluia!

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Where the Paschal blood is poured,
Death's dark angel sheathes his sword;
Israel's hosts triumphant go Through the wave that drowns the foe.
Alleluia!

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Praise we Christ, whose blood was shed,
Paschal Victim,
Pas* chal Bread;
With sincerity and love Eat we Manna from above.
Alleluia!

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Mighty Victim from the sky,
Hell's fierce pow'rs beneath Thee lie;
Thou hast conquered in the fight,
Thou hast brought us life and light;
Alleluia!

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: Now no more can death appall,
Now no more the grave enthrall;
Thou hast opened Paradise,
And in Thee Thy saints shall rise.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: Paschal triumph, Easter joy,
This alone can sin destroy;
From sin's death do Thou set free
Souls reborn, O Lord, in Thee.

blocks.label: Verse 8
lines: Hymns of glory and of praise,
Father, to Thee we raise;
Risen Lord, all praise to Thee,
Ever with the Spirit be.

title: Author of All Life
author: Brian James Dumont

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Author of all Life, our Fa* ther, breathe into our hearts again.
Stir our deadness, heal our weak* ness, crush our evil thoughts so vain.
Life Creator, life Redeemer, life Imparter,
Source of Truth,
Teach us now to love each o* ther,
Teach us Lord to love like You.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Hearts so hard, we hate each o* ther, those in need we treat with scorn...
Old, unwise, or not my col* or,
Palsied limbs, or not yet born.
Life Creator, life Redeemer, life Imparter,
Three in One,
Teach us Lord to see Your I* mage,
Teach us now to see the Son.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Christ now grants us life eter* nal, to know You the one true God,
He the Way to see the Fa* ther,
He the One who felt the rod.
Life Creator, life Redeemer, life Imparter,
Life conferred!
Let us sing of Your atone* ment,
Let all people hear Your Word!

title: Awake, My Heart, With Gladness
author: Paul Gerhardt

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Awake, my heart, with gladness,
See what today is done;
How after gloom and sadness,
Comes forth the glo* rious Sun.
My Savior there was laid Where our bed must be made When to the realms of light Our spi* rit wings its flight.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: They in the grave did sink Him,
The foe held ju* bilee;
Before he can bethink him,
Lo!
Christ again is free.
And "Victory" He cries,
And waving tow'rds the skies His ban* ner, while the field Is by the He* ro held!

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Upon the grave is standing The He* ro look* ing round;
The foe, no more withstanding,
His wea* pons on the ground Throws down, his hell* ish pow'r To Christ must he give o'er,
And to the Vic* tor's bands Must yield his feet and hands.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: A sight it is to gladden;
And fill the heart with glee,
No more affright or sadden Shall aught, or take from me My trust or for* titude,
Or any prec* ious good The Sa* vior bought for me In sov'r* eign love and free.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Hell and its prince, the devil,
Of all their pow'rs are shorn;
Now I am safe from evil,
And sin I laugh to scorn.
Grim Death with all his might Cannot my soul affright;
He is a pow'r* less form,
Howe'er he rage and storm.

title: Awake My Soul, An Offering Bring
author: Brian L. Penney

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Awake my soul, an off'ring bring to Jesus our exalted King;
Sing to Him Who reigns above in carnate fount of grace and love;
Sing to Him Who reigns above incarnate fount of grace and love.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: In awe we stand upon this ground,
His wisdom and His pow'r astound;
All His wonders we behold, in heav'n and earth His story's told;
All His wonders we behold, in heav'n and earth His story's told.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Then to this world, behold what grace!
He comes to rescue Adam's race;
Our Redeemer, our High Priest, from sin and death He brings release;
Our Redeemer, our High Priest, from sin and death He brings release.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Awake my soul, arise and sing, eternal praise to Christ our King;
In His Church,
His Name confessed, we worship Him among the blessed;
In His Church,
His Name confessed, we worship Him among the blessed.

title: Awake, My Soul, And With The Sun
author: Thomas Ken

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Awake, my soul, and with the sun Thy daily stage of duty run;
Shake off dull sloth, and joyful rise,
To pay thy morning sacrifice.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Thy precious time misspent, redeem,
Each present day thy last esteem,
Improve thy talent with due care;
For the great day thyself prepare.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: By influence of Light divine Let thy own light to others shine.
Reflect all Heaven's propitious ways In ardent love, and cheerful praise.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: In conversation be sincere;
Keep conscience as the noontide clear;
Think how all seeing God thy ways And all thy secret thoughts surveys.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Wake, and lift up thyself, my heart,
And with the angels bear thy part,
Who all night long unwearied sing High praise to the eternal King.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: All praise to Thee, Who safe has kept
And hast refreshed me while I slept
Grant, Lord, when I from death shall wake
I may of endless light partake.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: Heav'n is, dear Lord, where'er Thou art,
O never then from me depart;
For to my soul 'tis hell to be
But for one moment void of Thee.

blocks.label: Verse 8
lines: Lord, I my vows to Thee renew;
Disperse my sins as morning dew.
Guard my first springs of thought and will,
And with Thyself my spirit fill.

blocks.label: Verse 9
lines: Direct, control, suggest, this day,
All I design, or do, or say,
That all my powers, with all their might,
In Thy sole glory may unite.

blocks.label: Verse 10
lines: I would not wake nor rise again
And Heaven itself I would disdain,
Wert Thou not there to be enjoyed,
And I in hymns to be employed.

blocks.label: Verse 11
lines: Praise God, from Whom all blessings flow;
Praise Him, all creatures here below;
Praise Him above, ye heavenly host;
Praise Father, Son, and Holy Ghost.

title: Away In A Manger
author: John T. anonymous;MacFarland

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Away in a manger, no crib for a bed,
The little Lord Jesus laid down His sweet head.
The stars in the sky looked down where He lay,
The little Lord Jesus, asleep on the hay.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: The cattle are lowing, the Baby awakes,
But little Lord Jesus, no crying He makes;
I love Thee,
Lord Jesus, look down from the sky And stay by my cradle til morning is nigh.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Be near me,
Lord Jesus,
I ask Thee to stay Close by me for ever, and love me,
I pray;
Bless all the dear children in Thy tender care,
And fit us for Heaven to live with Thee there.

title: Baptized Into Thy Name Most Holy
author: Johann Jakob Rambach

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Baptized into Thy Name most holy,
O Father,
Son, and Holy Ghost,
I claim a place, though weak and lowly,
Among Thy seed,
Thy chosen host.
Buried with Christ and dead to sin,
Thy Spirit now shall live within.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: My loving Father, here doth take me To be henceforth His child and heir;
My faithful Savior, now doth make me The fruit of all His sorrows share;
My Comforter will comfort me When darkest clouds around I see.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: And I have vowed to fear and love Thee And to obey Thee,
Lord, alone;
I felt Thy Holy Spirit move me,
I dared to pledge myself Thine own,
Renouncing sin to keep the faith And war with evil unto death.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: My faithful God,
Thou failest never,
Thy cov'nant surely will abide;
Oh, cast me not away forever Should I transgress it on my side!
But if I fall hide not Thy face,
Restore Thy child,
Lord, by Thy Grace.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Yes, all I am and love most dearly,
To Thee I offer now the whole;
O let me make my vows sincerely,
Take full possession of my soul!
Let naught within me, naught I own,
Serve any will save Thine alone.

title: Be Still My Soul
author: Katharina Amalia Dorothea von Schlegel

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Be still, my soul: the Lord is on thy side.
Bear patiently the cross of grief or pain.
Leave to thy God to order and provide;
In every change,
He faithful will remain.
Be still, my soul: thy best, thy heav'nly Friend Through thorny ways leads to a joyful end.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Be still, my soul: thy God doth undertake To guide the fu ture, as He has the past.
Thy hope, thy confidence let nothing shake;
All now mysterious shall be bright at last.
Be still, my soul: the waves and winds still know His voice Who ruled them while He dwelt below.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Be still, my soul: when dearest friends depart,
And all is dark ened in the vale of tears,
Then shalt thou better know His love,
His heart,
Who comes to soothe thy sorrow and thy fears.
Be still, my soul: thy Je sus can repay From His own fullness all He takes away.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Be still, my soul: the hour is hast'ning on When we shall be forever with the Lord.
When disappointment, grief and fear are gone,
Sorrow forgot, love's purest joys restored.
Be still, my soul: when change and tears are past All safe and bless�d we shall meet at last.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Be still, my soul: begin the song of praise On earth, believ ing, to Thy Lord on high;
Acknowledge Him in all thy words and ways,
So shall He view thee with a well pleased eye.
Be still, my soul: the Sun of life divine Through passing clouds shall but more brightly shine.

title: Be Thou My Vision
author: Dallan Forgaill

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Be Thou my Vision,
O Lord of my heart;
Naught be all else to me, save that Thou art.
Thou my best Thought, by day or by night,
Waking or sleep* ing,
Thy presence my light.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Be Thou my Wisdom, and Thou my true Word;
I ever with Thee and Thou with me,
Lord;
Thou my great Father, and I Thy true son;
Thou in me dwell* ing, and I with Thee one.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Be Thou my battle Shield,
Sword for the fight;
Be Thou my Dignity,
Thou my Delight;
Thou my soul's Shelter,
Thou my high Tower: Raise Thou me heav'n* ward,
O Pow'r of my pow'r.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Riches I heed not, nor man's empty praise,
Thou mine Inheritance, now and always: Thou and Thou only, be first in my heart,
High King of Hea* ven, my Treasure Thou art.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: High King of Heaven, my victory won,
May I reach Heav'ns joys,
O bright Heaven's Sun!
Heart of my own heart, whatever befall,
Still be my Vi* sion,
O Ruler of all.

title: Beautiful Savior (Fairest Lord Jesus)
author: German Jesuits

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Beautiful Sa* vior,
King of Crea* tion Son of God and Son of Man!
Truly I'd love Thee, truly I'd serve Thee,
Light of my soul, my joy, my crown.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Fair are the mea* dows,
Fair are the wood* lands,
Robed in the flow'rs of blooming spring;
Jesus is fair* er,
Jesus is pur* er,
He makes our sorr'wing spirit sing.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Fair is the sun* shine,
Fair is the moon* light,
Bright the sparkling stars on high;
Jesus shines bright* er,
Jesus shines pur* er Than all the angels in the sky.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Beautiful Sa* vior,
Lord of the na* tions,
Son of God and Son of Man!
Glory and ho* nor,
Praise, adora* tion Now and forevermore be Thine!

title: Behold, A Host, Arrayed in White
author: Hans Adolf Brorson

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Be* hold a host, arrayed in white,
Like thousand snow clad mountains bright,
With palms they stand.
Who is this band Be* fore the throne of light?
Lo, these are they of glo* rious fame Who from the great a* ffliction came And in the flood of Je* sus' blood Are cleansed from guilt and blame.
Now gathered in the ho* ly place Their voices they in worship raise,
Their an* thems swell where God doth dwell,
Mid an* gels song of praise.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Des* pised and scorned, they so* journed here;
But now, how glo* rious they appear!
Those mar* tyrs stand a priest* ly band,
God's throne forev* er near.
So oft, in troubled days gone by,
In anguish they would weep and sigh.
At home a* bove the God of Love For aye their tears shall dry.
They now enjoy their Sab* bath rest,
The paschal ban* quet of the blest;
The Lamb, their Lord, at fest* al board Him* self is Host and Guest.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Then hail, ye mighty le* gions, yea,
All hail!
Now safe and blest for aye,
And praise the Lord, who with His Word Sus* tained you on the way.
Ye did the joys of earth dis* dain,
Ye toiled and sowed in tears and pain.
Fare* well, now bring your sheaves and sing Sal* va* tion's glad refrain.
Swing high your palms, lift up your song,
Yea, make it my* riad voices strong.
E* ter* nally shall praise to Thee,
God, and the Lamb belong.

title: Beneath The Cross Of Jesus
author: Elizabeth Cecelia Douglas Clephane

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Beneath the cross of Jesus I fain would take my stand,
The shadow of a mighty rock within a weary land;
A home within the wilderness, a rest upon the way,
From the burning of the noontide heat, and the burden of the day.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: O safe and happy shelter,
O refuge tried and sweet,
O trysting place where Heaven's love and Heaven's justice meet!
As to the holy patriarch that wondrous dream was giv'n,
So seems my Savior's cross to me, a ladder up to heav'n.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: There lies beneath its shadow but on the further side The darkness of an awful grave that gapes both deep and wide And there between us stands the cross two arms outstretched to save A watchman set to guard the way from that eternal grave.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Upon that cross of Jesus mine eye at times can see The very dying form of One Who suffered there for me;
And from my stricken heart with tears two wonders I confess;
The wonders of redeeming love and my unworthiness.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: I take,
O cross, thy shadow for my abiding place;
I ask no other sunshine than the sunshine of His face;
Content to let the world go by to know no gain or loss,
My sinful self my only shame, my glory all the cross.

title: Blessed Assurance
author: Fanny Jane Crosby

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Bless�d assurance,
Jesus is mine!
O what a foretaste of glory divine!
Heir of salvation, purchase of God,
Born of His Spirit, washed in His blood.
This is my story, this is my song,
Praising my Savior, all the day long;

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Perfect submission, perfect delight,
Visions of rapture now burst on my sight;
Angels descending bring from above Echoes of mercy, whispers of love.
This is my story, this is my song,
Praising my Savior, all the day long.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Perfect submission, all is at rest I in my Savior am happy and blest,
Watching and waiting, looking above,
Filled with His goodness, lost in His love.

title: Blessed Jesus at Thy Word
author: Tobias Clausnitzer

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Blessed Jesus, at Thy Word We are gathered all to hear Thee;
Let our hearts and souls be stirred Now to seek and love and fear Thee,
By Thy teachings sweet and holy,
Drawn from earth to love Thee solely.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: All our knowledge, sense, and sight Lie in deepest darkness shrouded,
Til Thy Spirit breaks our night With the beams of truth unclouded;
Thou alone to God canst win us;
Thou must work all good within us.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Glorious Lord,
Thyself impart!
Light of light, from God proceeding,
Open Thou our ears and heart;
Help us by Thy Spirit's pleading;
Hear the cry Thy people raises;
Hear and bless our prayers and praises.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Father,
Son, and Holy Ghost,
Praise to Thee and adoration!
Grant that we Thy Word may trust And obtain true consolation,
While we here below must wander,
Till we sing Thy praises yonder.

title: Blest Be The Tie That Binds
author: John Fawcett

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Blest be the tie that binds Our hearts in Christian love;
The fellowship of kindred minds Is like to that above.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Before our Father's throne We pour our ardent prayers;
Our fears, our hopes, our aims are one Our comforts and our cares.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: We share each other's woes,
Our mutual burdens bear;
And often for each other flows The sympathizing tear.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: When we asunder part,
It gives us inward pain;
But we shall still be joined in heart,
And hope to meet again.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: This glorious hope revives Our courage by the way;
While each in expectation lives,
And longs to see the day.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: From sorrow, toil and pain,
And sin, we shall be free,
And perfect love and friendship reign
Through all eternity.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Blind Bar* timaeus at the gates Of Jericho in darkness waits: He hears the crowd;
he hears a breath say "It is Christ of Nazareth!" And calls in tones of agony, "O Jesus,
Je* sus pity me!"

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: The throng* ing multitudes in-crease "Blind Bartimae* us, hold thy peace!" But still, above the noisy crowd,
The blind man's cry is shrill and loud: Until they say, "He calleth thee;
Courage!
arise!
He calleth thee!"

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Then saith the Christ, as silent stands The crowd, "What wilt thou at My hands?" And he replies, "O give me light!
Rabbi, restore the blind man's sight." And Je* sus an swers, "Go thy way,
Thy faith, thy faith hath sav�d thee."

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Ye that hath eyes and cannot see,
In darkness and in misery,
Recall those migh* ty voices three "O Jesus,
Je* sus pity me!" "Courage!
arise!
He calleth thee!" "Thy faith, thy faith hath sav�d thee."

title: Breathe on Me, Breath of God
author: Edwin Hatch

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Breathe on me, breath of God,
Fill me with life anew,
That I may love what Thou dost love,
And do what Thou wouldst do.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Breathe on me, breath of God,
Until my heart is pure,
Until with Thee I will one will,
To do and to endure.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Breathe on me, breath of God,
So shall I never die,
But live with Thee the perfect life Of Thine eternity.

title: Built on the Rock
author: Nikolai Frederik Severin Grundtvig

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Built on the Rock the church doth stand,
Even when steeples are fall ing;
Crumbled have spires in every land,
Bells still are chiming and calling;
Calling the young and old to rest,
But above all the soul distressed,
Longing for rest everlasting.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Surely in temples made with hands,
God, the Most High, is not dwell ing;
High above earth His temple stands,
All earthly temples excelling;
Yet He whom heav'ns cannot contain Chose to abide on earth with men,
Built in our bodies His temple.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: We are God's house of living stones,
Built for His own habita tion;
He through baptismal grace us owns,
Heirs of His wondrous salvation;
Were we but two His Name to tell,
Yet He would deign with us to dwell,
With all His grace and His favor.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Now we may gather with our King;
Ev'n in the lowliest dwell ing: Praises to Him we there may bring,
His wondrous mercy foretelling;
Jesus His grace to us accords,
Spirit and life are all His words,
His truth doth hallow the temple.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Still we our earthly temples rear,
That we may herald His prais es;
They are the homes where He draws near And little children embraces,
Beautiful things in them are said,
God there with us His cov'nant made,
Making us heirs of His kingdom.

title: By Grace I'm Saved
author: Christian Ludwig Scheidt

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: By grace I'm savedgrace free and boundless!
My heart, believ'st thou this or not?
Why tremblest thou with terror groundless?
Has ever God a falsehood taught?
His Word is truethen this must be: By grace there is a crown for thee.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: By grace!
our works are all rejected,
All claims of merit pass for naught;
The mighty Savior, long expected,
To us this blissful truth has brought,
That He by death redeems our race,
And we are saved alone by grace.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: By grace!
mark well this phrase's meaning,
When sin rolls sorrows o'er thy breast,
When Satan threats with pride o'erweening,
When troubled conscience sighs for rest: What reason ne'er can comprehend It pleases God by grace to send.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: By grace His Son, on earth appearing,
Vouchsafed beneath thy woe to bend;
Hadst thou, damnation justly fearing,
Done aught to render Him thy friend?
Was't not that He thy welfare sought,
And but by grace deliv'rance wrought?

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: By grace!
this ground of our salvation As long as God is true endures: What saints have penned by inspiration,
What God to our poor soul secures,
What all our faith must rest upon,
Is grace, free grace through His dear Son.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: By grace! but think not, thou who livest
Securely on in godless ways,
That thou, though all are called, receivest
The promised rest that wakes our praise:
By grace none find in heaven a place
Who live in sin in hope of grace.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: By grace! They who have heard this sentence
Must bid hypocrisy farewell;
For only after deep repentance
The soul what grace imports can tell;
To sin while grace a trifle seems,
To faith it bright with glory beams.

blocks.label: Verse 8
lines: By grace the timid hearts that languish,
Find access to the Father's heart,
When conflicts fierce and bitter anguish
Bid all their joy and hopes depart.
Where, oftimes, should I strength obtain,
Bid grace my anchor not remain!

blocks.label: Verse 9
lines: By grace! on this in death I'll rest me,
Rejoicing e'en though feeling naught;
I know my sin it oft oppressed me
But Him, too, who my soul hath bought:
My heart exults grief flees apace
Because my soul is saved by grace.

blocks.label: Verse 10
lines: By grace! O sin and Satan hear it!
I bear my flag of faith in hand,
And pass, in spite of doubts, nor fear it,
The Red Sea to the promised land;
I hold the word my Savior taught
As certain, whether felt or not.

Tell her that her sins I cover,
And her warfare now is over.

lines: For the herald's voice is crying In the desert far and near,
Bidding all men to repentance,

O that warning cry obey!
Now prepare for God a way!
Let the valleys rise to meet Him,
And the hills bow down to greet Him.

lines: Yea, her sins our God will pardon,

For the glory of the Lord O'er the earth is shed abroad,

While angels sing, with pious mirth,

Wher* e'er I turn my eye;
If I sur* vey the ground I tread,
Or gaze upon the sky.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: There's not a plant or flow'r below,
But makes Thy glories known;
And clouds a* rise and tempests blow,
By or* der from Thy throne.
Crea* tures that borrow life from Thee Are subject to Thy care: There's not a place where we can flee,
But God is present there.

title: If God Had Not Been on Our Side (Had God not Come, May Israel Say or Were God Not With Us At This Time)
author: Martin Luther

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: If God had not been on our side And had not come to aid us,
The foes with all their pow'r and pride Would surely have dismayed us;
For we,
His flock, would have to fear The threat of men both far and near Who rise in might against us.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Their furious wrath, did God permit,
Would surely have consumed us And as a deep and yawning pit With life and limb entombed us.
Like men o'er whom dark waters roll Their wrath would have en gulfed our soul And, like a flood, o'erwhelmed us.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Blest be the Lord, who foiled their threat That they could not devour us;
Our souls, like birds, escaped their net,
They could not overpow'r us.
The snare is broken we are free!
Our help is ever,
Lord, in Thee,
Who madest earth and hea* ven.

title: If God Himself Be For Me
author: Paul Gerhardt

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: If God Himself be for me,
I may a host defy;
For when I pray, before me My foes, confounded, fly.
If Christ, my Head and Master,
Befriend me from above,
What foe or what disas* ter Can drive me from His love?

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: This I believe, yea, ra* ther,
Of this I make my boast,
That God is my dear Fa* ther,
The Friend who loves me most,
And that, whate'er betide me,
My Savior is at hand Through stormy seas to guide me And bring me safe to land.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: I build on this founda* tion,
That Jesus and His blood Alone are my salva* tion,
The true, eternal good.
Without Him all that pleases Is valueless on earth;
The gifts I owe to Je* sus Alone my love are worth.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: My Jesus is my Splen* dor,
My Sun, my Light, alone;
Were He not my Defen* der Before God's awefull throne,
I never should find favor And mercy in His sight,
But be destroyed forev* er As darkness by the light.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: He canceled my offen* ses,
Delivered me from death;
He is the Lord who clean* ses My soul from sin through faith.
In Him I can be cheerful,
Bold, and undaunted aye;
In Him I am not fear* ful Of God's great Judgment Day.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: Naught, naught, can now condemn me Nor set my hope aside;
Now hell no more can claim me, Its fury I deride.
No sentence e'er reproves me, No ill destroys my peace;
For Christ, my Savior, loves me And shields me with His grace.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: His Spirit in me dwelleth, And o'er my mind He reigns.
All sorrow He dispelleth And soothes away all pains.
He crowns His work with blessing And helpeth me to cry,
"My Father!" without ceasing, To Him who dwells on high.

blocks.label: Verse 8
lines: And when my soul is lying Weak, trembling, and opprest,
He pleads with groans and sighing That cannot be exprest;
But God's quick eye discerns them, Although they give no sound,
And into language turns them E'en in the heart's deep ground.

blocks.label: Verse 9
lines: To mine His Spirit speaketh Sweet word of holy cheer,
How God to him that seeketh For rest is always near
And how He hath erected A city fair and new,
Where what our faith expected We evermore shall view.

blocks.label: Verse 10
lines: In yonder home doth flourish My heritage, my lot;
Though here I die and perish, My heaven shall fail me not.
Though care my life oft saddens And causeth tears to flow,
The light of Jesus gladdens And sweetens every woe.

blocks.label: Verse 11
lines: Who clings with resolution To Him whom Satan hates
Must look for persecution; For him the burden waits
Of mockery, shame, and losses, Heaped on his blameless head;
A thousand plagues and crosses Will be his daily bread.

blocks.label: Verse 12
lines: From me this is not hidden, Yet I am not afraid;
I leave my cares, as bidden, To whom my vows were paid.
Though life and limb it cost me And everything I won,
Unshaken shall I trust Thee And cleave to Thee alone.

blocks.label: Verse 13
lines: Though earth be rent asunder, Thou'rt mine eternally;
Not fire nor sword nor thunder Shall sever me from Thee;
Not hunger, thirst, nor danger, Not pain nor poverty
Nor mighty princes' anger Shall ever hinder me.

blocks.label: Verse 14
lines: No angel and no gladness, No throne, no pomp, no show,
No love, no hate, no sadness, No pain, no depth of woe,
No scheme of man's contrivance, However small or great,
Shall draw me from Thy guidance Nor from Thee separate.

blocks.label: Verse 15
lines: My heart for joy is springing And can no more be sad,
'Tis full of mirth and singing, Sees naught but sunshine glad.
The Sun that cheers my spirit Is Jesus Christ, my King;
That which I shall inherit Makes me rejoice and sing.

title: I'm But A Stranger Here
author: Thomas Rawson Taylor

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: I'm but a stranger here,
Heav'n is my home;
Earth is a desert drear,
Heav'n is my home.
Danger and sorrow stand round me on every hand;
Heav'n is my fatherland,
Heav'n is my home.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: What though the tempest rage,
Heav'n is my home;
Short is my pilgrimage,
Heav'n is my home;
Time's wild and wintry blast soon shall be over past;
I shall reach home at last,
Heav'n is my home.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: There at my Savior's side Heav'n is my home;
I shall be glorified,
Heav'n is my home.
There are the good and blest, those I loved most and best;
There, too,
I soon shall rest,
Heav'n is my home.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Therefore I murmur not,
Heav'n is my home;
Whate'er my earthly lot,
Heav'n is my home;
And I shall surely stand there at my Lord's right hand.
Heav'n is my fatherland,
Heav'n is my home.

title: Immortal, Invisible, God Only Wise
author: Walter Chalmers Smith

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Immortal, invisible,
God only wise,
In light inaccessible hid from our eyes,
Most bless�d, most glorious, the Ancient of Days,
Almighty, victorious,
Thy great Name we praise.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Unresting, unhasting, and silent as light,
Nor wanting, nor wasting,
Thou rulest in might;
Thy justice, like mountains, high soaring above Thy clouds, which are fountains of goodness and love.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: To all, life Thou givest, to both great and small;
In all life Thou livest, the true life of all;
We blossom and flourish as leaves on the tree,
And wither and perish but naught changeth Thee.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Great Father of glory, pure Father of light,
Thine angels adore Thee, all veiling their sight;
But of Thy rich graces this grace,
Lord, impart Take the veil from our face, the vile from our heart.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: All laud we would render;
O help us to see 'Tis only the splendor of light hideth Thee,
And so let Thy glory, almighty, impart,
Through Christ in His story,
Thy Christ to the heart.

title: In His Temple Now Behold Him
author: Henry John Pye

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: In His temple now behold Him,
See the long expected Lord;
Ancient prophets had foretold Him;
God has now fulfilled His word.
Now to praise Him,
His redeem�d Shall break forth with one accord.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: In the arms of her who bore Him,
Virgin pure, behold Him lie,
While his ag�d saints adore Him Ere in faith and hope they die.
Hallelujah!
Hallelujah!
Lo, th'incarnate God most high.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Jesus, by Thy presentation,
Thou, who didst for us endure,
Make us see our great salvation,
Seal us with Thy pro* mise sure.
And present us in Thy glory To Thy Father, cleansed and pure.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Prince and Author of salvation,
Be Thy bound* less love our theme!
Jesus, praise to Thee be given By the world Thou didst redeem.
With the Father and the Spirit,
Lord of majesty supreme!

title: In Peace and Joy I Now Depart (The Song of Simeon: Nunc Dimitis)
author: Martin Luther

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: In peace and joy I now depart At God's dispos* ing;
For full of comfort is my heart,
Soft repos* ing.
So the Lord hath pro* mised me,
And death is but a slum* ber.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: 'Tis Christ that wrought this work for me,
My faithful Sa* vior,
Whom Thou hast made mine eyes to see By Thy fa* vor.
Now I know He is my Life,
My Help in need and dy* ing.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Him Thou hast unto all set forth Their great Salva* tion And to His kingdom called the earth,
Every na* tion,
By Thy dear and whole* some Word,
In every place resound* ing.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: He is the Hope and saving Light Of lands benight* ed;
By Him are they who dwelt in night Fed and light* ed.
He is Is* rael's Praise and Bliss,
Their Joy,
Reward, and Glor* y.

title: In The Bleak MidWinter
author: Christina Georgina Rossetti

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: In the bleak midwin* ter, frosty wind made moan,
Earth stood hard as i* ron, water like a stone;
Snow had fallen, snow on snow, snow on snow on snow,
In the bleak midwinter, long ago.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Our God,
Heav'n cannot hold Him, nor earth sustain;
Heav'n and earth shall flee away when He comes to reign.
In the bleak midwin* ter a stable place sufficed The Lord God Almighty,
Je* sus Christ.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Enough for Him, whom cherubim, worship night and day,
Breast* ful of milk, and a mangerful of hay;
En- ough for Him, whom an* gels fall down before,
Ox and ass and camel which adore.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Angels and archan* gels may have gathered there,
Cherubim and seraphim thronged the air;
But His mother on* ly, in her maiden bliss,
Worshiped the beloved with a kiss.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: What can I give Him, poor as I am?
If I were a shep* herd,
I would bring a lamb;
If I were a Wise Man,
I would do my part;
Yet what can I give Him: give my heart.

title: In These Our Days So Perilous (Grant Peace, We Pray, in Mercy, Lord or Grant Peace in Mercy, Lord, We Pray)
author: Martin Latin;Luther

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: In these our days so perilous,
Lord, peace in mercy send us;
No God but Thee can fight for us,
No God but Thee defend us;
Thou our only God and Sa* vior.

title: Isaiah, Mighty Seer, In Days of Old (These Things the Seer Isaiah did Befall or Isaiah 'twas the Prophet)
author: Martin Luther

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Isaiah, mighty seer, in days of old The Lord of all in Spirit did behold High on a lofty throne, in splendor bright,
With flowing train that filled the Temple quite.
Above the throne were stately seraphim,
Six wings had they, these messengers of Him.
With twain they veiled their faces, as was meet,
With twain in reverent awe they hid their feet,
And with the other twain aloft they soared,
One to the other called and praised the Lord: "Holy is God, the Lord of Sabaoth!
Holy is God, the Lord of Sabaoth!
Holy is God, the Lord of Sabaoth!
Behold,
His glory filleth all the earth!" The beams and lintels trembled at the cry,
And clouds of smoke enwrapped the throne on high.

title: It Came Upon A Midnight Clear
author: Edmund Hamilton Sears

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: It came upon the midnight clear,
That glor* ious song of old,
From angels bend* ing near the earth,
To touch their harps of gold;
"Peace on the earth, good will to men,
From Heaven's all gra* cious King." The world in so* lemn stillness lay,
To hear the an* gels sing.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Still through the clo* ven skies they come With peace* ful wings unfurled,
And still their heavenly music floats O'er all the wea* ry world;
Above its sad and lowly plains,
They bend on hov* 'ring wing,
And ever over its Babel sounds The bless�d an* gels sing.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Yet with the woes of sin and strife The world has suf* fered long;
Beneath the an* gel strain have rolled Two thousand years of wrong;
And man, at war with man, hears not The love* song which they bring;
O hush the noise, ye men of strife And hear the an* gels sing.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: And ye, beneath life's crushing load,
Whose forms are bend* ing low,
Who toil along the climbing way With painful steps and slow,
Look now!
for glad and golden hours Come swift* ly on the wing.
O rest beside the weary road,
And hear the an* gels sing!

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: For lo!
the days are hast'ning on,
By pro* phetbards foretold,
When with the ev* er circling years Comes round the age of gold;
When peace shall ov* er all the earth Its an* cient splen* dors fling,
And the whole world send back the song Which now the an* gels sing.

title: It Is Well With My Soul (When Peace Like a River)
author: Horatio Gates Spafford

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: When peace, like a river, atten* deth my way,
When sorrows like sea billows roll;
Whatever my lot,
Thou has taught me to say,
It is well, it is well, with my soul.
It is well, with my soul,
It is well, it is well with my soul.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Though Satan should buffet, though tri* als should come,
Let this blest assurance control,
That Christ has regarded my helpless es tate,
And hath shed His own blood for my soul.
It is well, with my soul,

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: My sin, oh, the bliss of this glo* rious thought!
My sin, not in part but the whole,
Is nailed to the cross, and I bear it no more,
Praise the Lord, praise the Lord,
O my soul!

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: For me, be it Christ, be it Christ hence to live: If Jordan above me shall roll,
No pang shall be mine, for in death as in life Thou wilt whisper Thy peace to my soul.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: But,
Lord, 'tis for Thee, for Thy com* ing we wait,
The sky, not the grave, is our goal;
Oh trump of the angel!
Oh voice of the Lord!
Bless�d hope, bless�d rest of my soul!

title: Jerusalem the Golden
author: Bernard of Cluny aka. Bernard of Morlaix

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Jerusalem the golden, with milk and honey blest,
Beneath thy contemplation sink heart and voice oppressed.
I know not,
O I know not, what joys await us there,
What radiancy of glory, what bliss beyond compare.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: They stand, those halls of Zion, all jubilant with song,
And bright with many'an angel, and all the martyr throng;
The Prince is ever in them, the daylight is serene.
The pastures of the bless�d are decked in glorious sheen.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: There is the throne of David, and there, from care released,
The shout of them that triumph, the song of them that feast;
And they are with their Leader, who conquered in the fight,
And won for them forever their gleaming robes of white.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: O sweet and bless�d country, the home of God's elect!
O sweet and bless�d country, that eager hearts expect!
Jesus, in mercy bring us to that dear land of rest,
Who art, with God the Father, and Spirit, ever blessed.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Brief life is here our portion, brief sorrow, short lived care;
The life that knows no ending, the tearless life, is there.
O happy retribution!
Short toil, eternal rest;
For mortals and for sinners, a mansion with the blest.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: That we should look, poor wanderers, to have our home on high!
That worms should seek for dwellings beyond the starry sky!
And now we fight the battle, but then shall wear the crown
Of full and everlasting, and passionless renown.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: And how we watch and struggle, and now we live in hope,
And Zion in her anguish with Babylon must cope;
But he whom now we trust in shall then be seen and known,
And they that know and see Him shall have Him for their own.

blocks.label: Verse 8
lines: For thee, O dear, dear country, mine eyes their vigils keep;
For very love, beholding, thy happy name, they weep:
The mention of thy glory is unction to the breast,
And medicine in sickness, and love, and life, and rest.

blocks.label: Verse 9
lines: O one, O only mansion! O paradise of joy!
Where tears are ever banished, and smiles have no alloy;
The cross is all thy splendor, the Crucified thy praise,
His laud and benediction thy ransomed people raise.

blocks.label: Verse 10
lines: Jerusalem the glorious! Glory of the elect!
O dear and future vision that eager hearts expect!
E'en now by faith I see thee, e'en here thy walls discern;
To thee my thoughts are kindled, and strive, and pant, and yearn.

blocks.label: Verse 11
lines: Jerusalem, the only, that look'st from heaven below,
In thee is all my glory, in me is all my woe!
And though my body may not, my spirit seeks thee fain,
Till flesh and earth return me to earth and flesh again.

blocks.label: Verse 12
lines: Jerusalem, exulting on that securest shore,
I hope thee, wish thee, sing thee, and love thee evermore!
I ask not for my merit: I seek not to deny
My merit is destruction, a child of wrath am I.

blocks.label: Verse 13
lines: But yet with faith I venture and hope upon the way,
For those perennial guerdons I labor night and day.
The best and dearest Father Who made me, and Who saved,
Bore with me in defilement, and from defilement laved.

blocks.label: Verse 14
lines: When in His strength I struggle, for very joy I leap;
When in my sin I totter, I weep, or try to weep:
And grace, sweet grace celestial, shall all its love display,
And David's royal fountain purge every stain away.

blocks.label: Verse 15
lines: O sweet and bless�d country, shall I e'er see thy face?
O sweet and bless�d country, shall I e'er win thy grace?
I have the hope within me to comfort and to bless!
O shall I e'er win the prize? O tell me, tell me, Yes!

title: Jesus Came, the Heavens Adoring
author: Godfrey Thring

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Jesus came, the heav'ns adoring,
Came with peace from realms on high;
Jesus came for man's redemption,
Lowly came on earth to die.
Alleluia!
Alleluia!
Came in deep humility.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Jesus comes again in mercy,
When our hearts are bowed with care;
Jesus comes again in answer To an earnest, heartfelt prayer;
Alleluia!
Alleluia!
Comes to save us from despair.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Jesus comes to hearts rejoicing,
Bringing news of sins forgiv'n;
Jesus comes in sounds of gladness,
Leading souls redeemed to Heav'n;
Alleluia!
Alleluia!
Now the gate of death is riv'n.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Jesus comes in joy and sorrow,
Shares alike our hopes and fears;
Jesus comes, whate'er befalls us,
Glads our hearts, and dries our tears;
Alleluia!
Alleluia!
Cheering e'en our failing years.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Jesus comes on clouds triumphant,
When the heav'ns shall pass away;
Jesus comes again in glory;
Let us then our homage pay,
Alleluia!
Alleluia!
Till the dawn of endless day.

title: Jesus Christ Is Risen Today
author: Charles Bohemian;Wesley

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Jesus Christ is ris'n today,
Al* le* lu* ia!
Our triumphant holy day,
Al* le* lu* ia!
Who did once, upon the cross,
Al* le* lu* ia!
Suf* fer to redeem our loss,
Al* le* lu* ia!

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Hymns of praise then let us sing,
Al* le* lu* ia!
Unto Christ, our heav'nly King,
Al* le* lu* ia!
Who endured the cross and grave,
Al* le* lu* ia!
Sin* ners to redeem and save,
Al* le* lu* ia!

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: But the pain which He endured,
Al* le* lu* ia!
Our salvation hath procured,
Al* le* lu* ia!
Now above the sky He's king,
Al* le* lu* ia!
Where the angels ever sing,
Al* le* lu* ia!

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Sing we to our God above,
Al* le* lu* ia!
Praise eternal as His love,
Al* le* lu* ia!
Praise Him, all you heav'nly host,
Al* le* lu* ia!
Fa* ther,
Son, and Holy Ghost,
Al* le* lu* ia!

title: Jesus Christ, Our Blessed Savior
author: John Hus

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Jesus Christ, our Blessed Sav* ior,
Turned away God's wrath forev* er;
Suff'ring pains no tongue can tell,
He saved us from the pains of hell.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: To remind us that, to save us He hath died,
His flesh He gave us With this bread, a quick'ning food,
And with this wine,
His pre* cious blood.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Whoso to this board repair* eth,
Take good heed how He prepar* eth;
Death instead of life shall He Receive who comes unworth* ily.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Praise the Fa* ther,
God in hea* ven,
Who such dainty food hath gi* ven,
And for misdeeds thou hast done Gave to die His belov* ed Son.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Thou shalt hold with faith unshak* en,
That this food is to be tak* en By the sick who are distressed,
By those whose heart is sin* oppressed.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: To such grace and mercy turneth
Every soul that truly mourneth;
Art thou well? Avoid this board,
Else thou reapest an ill reward.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: Christ says: "Come ye heavy-laden,
I your weary hearts will gladden;
They that are yet strong  and well,
Despise the best physician's skill.

blocks.label: Verse 8
lines: Couldst thou earn thine own salvation,
Useless were my death and passion;
This feast is not spread for thee,
If thine own helper thou wilt be.

blocks.label: Verse 9
lines: If thou this believest truly,
And confession makest duly,
Thou a welcome guest art here,
This heavenly food thy soul shall cheer.

blocks.label: Verse 10
lines: But the fruits must not be missing,
Love thy neighbor without ceasing,
That true love let him receive,
Which here to thee thy God doth give.

title: Jesus Christ Who Came to Save
author: Martin Luther

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Jesus Christ, who came to save,
And overcame the grave,
Is now aris* en,
And sin hath bound in pri* son.
Kyri' elei* son.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Who withouten sin was found,
Bore our transgression's wound.
He is our Sa* vior,
And brings us to God's fa* vor.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Life and mercy, sin and death,
All in His hands He hath;
Them He'll deli* ver,
Who trust in Him forev* er.

title: Jesus Grant That Balm and Healing
author: Johann Heermann

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Jesus, grant that balm and healing In Thy holy wounds I find,
Every hour that I am feeling,
Pains of body and of mind.
Should some evil thought within Tempt my treacherous heart to sin,
Show the peril, and from sinning Keep me ere its first beginning.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Should some lust or sharp temp* tation Prove too strong for flesh and blood,
Let me think upon Thy Passion,
And the breach is soon made good.
Or should Satan press me hard,
Let me then be on my guard,
Saying, "Christ for me was wounded," That the tempter flee confounded.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: If the world my heart en* tices On the broad and easy road With its mirth and luring vices,
Let me think upon the load Thou didst carry and endure That I flee all thoughts impure,
Banishing each wild emotion,
Calm and blest in my devotion.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Every wound that pains or grieves me,
By Thy stripes,
Lord, is made whole;
When I'm faint,
Thy cross re* vives me,
Granting new life to my soul.
Yea,
Thy comfort renders sweet Every bitter cup I meet;
For Thy all atoning Passion Has procured my soul's salvation.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: O my God, my Rock and Tower,
Grant that in Thy death I trust,
Knowing death has lost his power Since Thou trodd'st him in the dust.
Savior, let Thine agony Ever help and comfort me;
When I die, be my Protection,
Light and Life and Resurrection.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: Jesus, grant that balm and healing In Thy holy wounds I find,
Every hour that I am feeling, Pains of body and of mind.
And when I this world must leave, Grant that, Lord, to Thee I cleave,
In Thy wounds find consolation And obtain my soul's salvation

title: Jesus, In Thy Dying Woes
author: Thomas Benson Pollock

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Jesus, in Thy dying woes,
Even while Thy lifeblood flows,
Craving pardon for Thy foes;
Hear us, holy Jesus.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Savior, for our pardon sue,
When our sins Thy pangs renew,
For we know not what we do: Hear us, holy Jesus.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: O may we, who mercy need,
Be like Thee in heart and deed,
When with wrong our spirits bleed: Hear us, holy Jesus.

title: Jesus Is All the World To Me
author: Will Lamartine Thompson

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Jesus is all the world to me,
My life, my joy, my all;
He is my strength from day to day,
Without Him I would fall.
When I am sad, to Him I go,
No other one can cheer me so;
When I am sad,
He makes me glad,
He's my friend.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Jesus is all the world to me, my friend in trials sore;
I go to Him for blessings and He gives them ov'r and o'er.
He sends the sunshine and the rain,
He sends the harvest's golden grain;
Sunshine and rain, harvest of grain,
He's my friend.

blocks.label: Verse 3

blocks.label: Verse 3

title: Lord Who Throughout These Forty Days (O Lord, Throughout These Forty Days)

blocks.label: Verse 5

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: May God bestow on us His grace,

title: Moment By Moment
author: Daniel Webster Whittle

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Dying with Jesus, by death reckoned mine;

Moment by moment,
O Lord,
I am Thine.
Moment by moment I'm kept in His love;
Moment by moment I've life from above;
Looking to

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Never a trial that He is not there,
Never a burden that He doth not bear,
Never a sorrow that He doth not share,
Moment by moment,
I'm under His care.
Jesus till glory doth shine;

O Lord,

blocks.label: Verse 3

More love to Thee;

O Christ, to Thee,
More love to Thee;
More love to Thee.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Once earthly joy I craved,

This all my pray'r shall be,
More love,
O Christ, to Thee,
More love to Thee;
More love to Thee.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Then shall my latest breath,

More love,
O Christ, to Thee,

title: My Faith Looks Up To Thee (My Faith Looks Trustingly)
