blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: While life's dark maze I tread,
And griefs around me spread, be Thou my Guide;
Bid darkness turn to day, wipe sorrow's tears away,
Nor let me ever stray from Thee aside.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: When ends life's transient dream,
When death's cold sullen stream over me roll;
Blest Savior, then in love, fear and dis trust remove;
O bear me safe above, a ransomed soul!

On Christ the solid

His covenant,
His blood,

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: When He shall come with trumpet sound,

lines: And, what of me, when I saw need?

lines: Sin bleeds from me and stops my breath, in Adam all I know is death;

how wonderful!
And my song shall ever be:

lines: For me it was in the garden He pray'd "Not my will, but Thine;" He had no tears for His own griefs,

O how marvelous!
O how wonderful!
And my song shall ever be:

How marvelous!
how wonderful!
Is my Savior's love for me!

blocks.label: Verse 4

no, not one!

no, not one!

no, not one!

no, not one!

lines: And is not mercy Thy prerogativeFree mercy, boundless, fathomless, divine?
Me,

lines: I hear Thy voice;
Thou bid'st me come and rest;
I come,
I kneel,
I clasp Thy pierc�d feet;

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Now thank we all our God, with heart and hands and voices,
Who wondrous things has done, in Whom this world rejoices;
Who from our mothers' arms has blessed us on our way With countless gifts of love, and still is ours today.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: O may this bounteous God through all our life be near us,
With ever joyful hearts and blessed peace to cheer us;
And keep us in His grace, and guide us when perplexed;
And free us from all ills, in this world and the next!

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: All praise and thanks to God the Father now be given;
The Son and Him Who reigns with Them in highest Heaven;
The one eternal God,
Whom earth and Heav'n adore;
For thus it was, is now, and shall be evermore.

title: Now the Light Has Gone Away
author: Frances Ridley Havergal

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Now the light has gone away;
Father, listen while I pray,
Asking Thee to watch and keep And to send me quiet sleep.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Jesus,
Savior, wash away All that has been wrong today;
Help me every day to be Good and gentle, more like Thee.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Let my near and dear ones be Always near and dear to Thee.
Oh, bring me and all I love To Thy happy home above.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Now my evening praise I give;
Thou didst die that I might live.
All my blessings come from Thee;
Oh, how good Thou art to me!

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Thou, my best and kindest Friend,
Thou wilt love me to the end.
Let me love Thee more and more,
Always better than before.

title: O Be Glad All Nations on Earth
author: Brian L. Penney

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: O be glad, all nations on Earth,
Come let Je* sus' Name be praised;
He is crowned, the King of glo* ry,
At God's right hand He is raised.
Angels bowing down before Him,
Singing with the heav'n* ly throng;
Elders cast* ing crowns before Him,
Sing* ing an eternal song.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Great and mar* velous are Your works,
Just and true are all Your ways;
All the na* tions bow in wor* ship,
King of kings,
Your Name they praise.
Angels bowing down before Him,
Singing with the heav'n* ly throng;
Elders cast* ing crowns before Him,
Sing* ing an eternal song.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: When shall Heav'n and Earth togeth* er,
Walk before the Lamb, its Light?
When shall all the saints be ga* thered, and that Day shall end the night?
Angels bowing down before Him,
Singing with the heav'n* ly throng;
Elders cast* ing crowns before Him,
Sing* ing an eternal song.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Lo, that day shall come with glo* ry,
When Christ comes with trumpet sound;
Then the saints will cease their groan* ing,
Nev* er more by death's chains bound.
Let us all bow down before Him,
Sing,
O sing th'e* ter* nal song;
Work in hope until we meet Him,
And we join the heav'nly throng.

title: O Chief of Cities Bethlehem
author: Aurelius Clemens Prudentius

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: O chief of cities,
Bethlehem,
Of David's crown the fairest gem,
But more to us than David's name,
In you, as man, the Savior came.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Beyond the sun in splendor bright,
Above you stands a wondrous light Proclaiming from the conscious skies That here, in flesh, the Godhead lies.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: The wise men, seeing Him so fair,
Bow low be fore Him, and with prayer Their treasured eastern gifts unfold Of incense, myrrh, and royal gold.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: The golden tribute owns Him King,
But frankin cense to God they bring,
And last, prophetic sign, with myrrh,
They shadow forth His sepulcher.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: O Jesus, whom the Gentiles see,
With Father,
Spi* rit,
One in Three: To You,
O God, be glory giv'n By saints on earth and saints in Heav'n.

title: O Come, All Ye Faithful
author: John Francis Wade

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: O come, all ye faithful, joyful and triumphant,
O come ye,
O come ye, to Beth* lehem.
Come and be hold Him, born the King of an* gels;
O come, let us a

blocks.label: Refrain
lines: dore Him,
O come, let us adore Him,
O come, let us adore Him,
Christ the Lord.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: True God of true God,
Light from Light Eternal,
Lo,
He shuns not the Vir* gin's womb;
Son of the Father, begotten, not created;

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Sing, choirs of angels, sing in exultation;
O sing, all ye citizens of heav'n above!
Glory to God, glory in the high* est;

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: See how the shepherds, summoned to His cradle,
Leaving their flocks, draw nigh to gaze;
We too will thither bend our joyful foot* steps;

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Lo!
star led chieftains,
Magi,
Christ adoring,
Offer Him in* cense, gold, and myrrh;
We to the Christ Child bring our hearts' obla* tions.

title: O Come O Come Emmanuel
author: unknown

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: O come,
O come,
Emman* uel,
And ransom captive Is* rael,
That mourns in lonely e* xile here Until the Son of God appear.

blocks.label: Refrain
lines: Rejoice!
Rejoice!
Emman* uel shall come to thee,
O I* srael.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: O come,
Thou Wisdom from on high,
Who orderest all things might* ily;
To us the path of know* ledge show,
And teach us in her ways to go.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: O come,
Thou Rod of Jes* se, free Thine own from Satan's ty* ranny;
From depths of hell Thy peo* ple save,
And give them vict'ry ov'r the grave.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: O come,
Thou Dayspring, come and cheer Our spirits by Thine ad* vent here;
Disperse the gloomy clouds of night,
And death's dark shadows put to flight.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: O come,
Thou Key of Da* vid, come,
And open wide our hea* v'nly home;
Make safe the way that leads on high,
And close the path to mi* sery.

title: O Day of Rest And Gladness
author: Christopher Wordsworth

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: O day of rest and glad* ness, o day of joy and light,
O balm of care and sad* ness, most beautiful, most bright: On thee, the high and lowly, through ages joined in tune,
Sing holy, holy, h* oly, to the great God Triune.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: On thee, at the crea* tion, the light first had its birth;
On thee, for our salva* tion,
Christ rose from depths of earth;
On thee, our Lord, victorious, the Spirit sent from heaven,
And thus on thee, most glor* ious, a triple light was given.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Thou art a port, protec* ted from storms that round us rise;
A garden, intersec* ted with streams of paradise;
Thou art a cool* ing fountain in life's dry, dreary sand;
From thee, like Pisgah's moun* tain, we view our promised land.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Thou art a holy lad* der, where angels go and come;
Each Sunday finds us glad* der, nearer to heaven, our home;
A day of sweet refection, thou art a day of love,
A day of resurrec* tion from earth to things above.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Today on weary na* tions the heavenly manna falls;
To holy convoca* tions the silver trumpet calls,
Where Gospel light is glowing with pure and radiant beams,
And living water flow* ing, with soul refreshing streams.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: New graces ever gaining from this our day of rest,
We reach the rest remaining to spirits of the blessed.
To Holy Ghost be praises, to Father, and to Son;
The church her voice upraises to Thee, blessed Three in One.

title: O Father, All Creating
author: John Ellerton

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: O Father, all creating,
Whose wisdom, love, and pow'r First bound two lives together In Eden's primal hour,
Today to these Thy children Thy earliest gifts renew: A home by Thee made happy,
A love by Thee kept true.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: O Savior,
Guest most bounteous Of old in Galilee,
Vouchsafe today Thy presence With these who call on Thee;
Their store of earthly gladness Transform to heav'nly wine,
And teach them, in the tasting To know the gift is Thine.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: O Spirit of the Father,
Breathe on them from above,
So mighty in Thy pureness,
So tender in Thy love;
That, guarded by Thy presence,
From sin and strife kept free,
Their lives may own Thy guidance,
Their hearts be rul'd by Thee.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Except Thou build it,
Father,
The house is built in vain;
Except Thou,
Savior, bless it,
The joy will turn to pain;
But naught can break the union Of hearts in Thee made one,
And love Thy Spirit hallow'd Is endless love begun.

title: O For A Thousand Tongues
author: Charles Wesley

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: O for a thousand tongues to sing My great Redeemer's praise,
The glories of my God and King,
The triumphs of His grace!

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: My gracious Master and my God,
Assist me to proclaim,
To spread through all the earth abroad The honors of Thy name.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Jesus!
the name that charms our fears,
That bids our sorrows cease;
'Tis music in the sinner's ears, 'Tis life, and health, and peace.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: He breaks the pow'r of canceled sin,
He sets the prisoner free;
His blood can make the foulest clean,
His blood availed for me.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: He speaks, and, listening to His voice,
New life the dead receive,
The mournful, broken hearts rejoice,
The humble poor believe.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: Hear Him, ye deaf; His praise, ye dumb,
Your loosened tongues employ;
Ye blind, behold your Savior come,
And leap, ye lame, for joy.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: In Christ your Head, you then shall know,
Shall feel your sins forgiven;
Anticipate your heaven below,
And own that love is heaven.

blocks.label: Verse 8
lines: Glory to God, and praise and love
Be ever, ever given,
By saints below and saints above,
The church in earth and heaven.

blocks.label: Verse 9
lines: On this glad day the glorious Sun
Of Righteousness arose;
On my benighted soul He shone
And filled it with repose.

blocks.label: Verse 10
lines: Sudden expired the legal strife,
'Twas then I ceased to grieve;
My second, real, living life
I then began to live.

blocks.label: Verse 11
lines: Then with my heart I first believed,
Believed with faith divine,
Power with the Holy Ghost received
To call the Savior mine.

blocks.label: Verse 12
lines: I felt my Lord's atoning blood
Close to my soul applied;
Me, me He loved, the Son of God,
For me, for me He died!

blocks.label: Verse 13
lines: I found and owned His promise true,
Ascertained of my part,
My pardon passed in heaven I knew
When written on my heart.

blocks.label: Verse 14
lines: Look unto Him, ye nations, own
Your God, ye fallen race;
Look, and be saved through faith alone,
Be justified by grace.

blocks.label: Verse 15
lines: See all your sins on Jesus laid:
The Lamb of God was slain,
His soul was once an offering made
For every soul of man.

blocks.label: Verse 16
lines: Awake from guilty nature's sleep,
And Christ shall give you light,
Cast all your sins into the deep,
And wash the �thiop white.

blocks.label: Verse 17
lines: Harlots and publicans and thieves
In holy triumph join!
Saved is the sinner that believes
From crimes as great as mine.

blocks.label: Verse 18
lines: Murderers and all ye hellish crew,
Ye sons of lust and pride,
Believe the Savior died for you;
For me the Savior died.

blocks.label: Verse 19
lines: With me, your chief, ye then shall know,
Shall feel your sins forgiven;
Anticipate your heaven below,
And own that love is heaven.

title: O Holy, Blessed Trinity
author: Martin Behm

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: O Holy,
Blessed Trinity,
Divine,
Essential Unity,
God Father,
Son, and Holy Ghost,
Be Thou this day my Guide and Host.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: My soul and body keep from harm,
O'er all I have extend Thine arm,
That Satan may not cause distress Nor bring me shame or wretchedness.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: The Father's might shield me this day,
The Son's pure wisdom cheer my way,
The Holy Spirit's light divine Illume my heart's benighted shrine.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: My Maker, strengthen Thou my heart,
O my Redeemer, help impart,
Blest Comforter, keep at my side That faith and love in me abide.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Lord, bless and keep Thou me as Thine;
Lord, make Thy face upon me shine;
Lord, lift Thy countenance on me And give me peacesweet peace, from Thee.

title: O Holy Spirit, Enter In
author: Michael Schirmer

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: O Holy Spirit, enter in,
And in our hearts Thy work begin Thy Temple deign to make us;
Sun of the soul,
Thou Light divine,
Around and in us brightly shine,
To joy and gladness wake us.
That we to Thee Truly living,
To Thee giving Prayer unceasing May in love be still increasing.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Give to Thy Word impressive pow'r That in our hearts, from this good hour,
As fire it may be glowing;
That we con fess the Father,
Son,
And Thee, the Spirit,
Three in One,
Thy glory ever showing.
Stay Thou, guide now Our souls ever that they never May forsake Thee.
But by faith their refuge make Thee.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Thou fountain whence all wisdom flows Which God on pious hearts bestows,
Grant us Thy consolation.
That in our pure faith's unity We faithful witnesses may be Of grace that brings salvation.
Hear us, cheer us,
By Thy teaching;
let our preaching,
And our labor Praise Thee,
Lord, and serve our neighbor.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Left to ourselves, we shall but stray;
O lead us on the narrow way,
With wisest counsel guide us;
And give us steadfastness, that we May ever faithful prove to Thee,
Whatever woes betide us;
Lord now Heal Thou All hearts broken,
And betoken Thou art near us,
Whom we trust to light and cheer us.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Thy heav'nly strength sustain our heart That we may act the valiant part With Thee as our Reliance;
Be Thou our Refuge and our Shield That we may never quit the field,
But stand in bold defiance.
Descend, defend From all errors And earth's terrors Thy salvation Be our constant consolation.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: O mighty Rock, O Source of life,
Let Thy dear Word 'mid doubt and strife
Be so within us burning,
That we be faithful unto death,
In Thy pure love and holy faith,
From Thee true wisdom learning!
Thy grace And peace
On us shower; By Thy power
Christ confessing,
Let us win our Savior's blessing.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: O gentle Dew, from Heav'n now fall
With pow'r upon the hearts of all,
Thy tender love instilling,
That heart to heart more closely bound,
Fruitful in kindly deeds be found,
The law of love fulfilling;
The Lord, Discord
Shall not grieve Thee; We recieve Thee;
Where Thou livest.
Peace, and love, and joy Thou givest.

blocks.label: Verse 8
lines: Grant that our days, while life shall last,
In purest holiness be passed,
Be Thou our Strength forever;
Grant that our hearts henceforth be free
From sinful lust and vanity
Which us from Thee must sever.
Keep Thou pure Now
From offenses Heart and senses.
Blessed Spirit!
Let us heavenly life inherit.

title: O Little Town of Bethlehem
author: Phillips Brooks

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: O little town of Bethlehem, how still we see thee lie!
Above thy deep and dreamless sleep the silent stars go by.
Yet in thy dark streets shineth the everlasting Light;
The hopes and fears of all the years are met in thee tonight.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: For Christ is born of Ma* ry, and gathered all above,
While mortals sleep, the angels keep their watch of wond'ring love.
O morning stars together, proclaim the holy birth,
And praises sing to God the King, and peace to men on earth!

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: How silently, how silently, the wondrous Gift is giv'n;
So God imparts to human hearts the blessings of His Heav'n.
No ear may hear His coming, but in this world of sin,
Where meek souls will receive Him still, the dear Christ enters in.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Where children pure and hap* py pray to the bless�d Child,
Where misery cries out to Thee,
Son of the mother mild;
Where charity stands watching and faith holds wide the door,
The dark night wakes, the glory breaks, and Christmas comes once more.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: O holy Child of Bethlehem, descend to us, we pray;
Cast out our sin, and enter in, be born in us today.
We hear the Christmas angels the great glad tidings tell;
O come to us, abide with us, our Lord Emmanuel!

title: O Lord, How Shall I Meet Thee
author: Paul Gerhardt

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: O Lord, how shall I meet Thee,
How welcome Thee aright?
All nations long to see Thee,
My Hope, my heart's Delight!
O kindle,
Lord, most holy,
Thy lamp within my breast,
To do in spirit lowly All that may please Thee best.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Thy Zion palms is strewing,
And branches fresh and fair;
My heart, its pow'rs renewing,
An anthem shall prepare.
My soul puts off her sadness Thy glories to proclaim;
With all her strength and gladness She fain would serve Thy Name.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: What hast Thou left ungranted To give me glad relief?
When soul and body panted In utmost depth of grief,
In deepest degradation,
Devoid of joy and peace,
Then,
Thou, my soul's Salvation,
Didst come to bring release.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: I lay in fetters groaning,
Thou com'st to set me free;
I stood, my shame bemoaning,
Thou com'st to honor me.
A glory Thou dost give me,
A treasure safe on high,
That will not fail nor leave me As earthly riches fly.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Love caused Thine incarnation Love brought Thee down to me;
Thy thirst for my salvation Procured my liberty.
O love beyond all telling,
That led Thee to embrace,
In love all love excelling,
Our lost and fallen race!

title: O Lord, I Am Not Worthy
author: 1777 from Landshuter Gesangbuch

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: O Lord,
I am not worthy That Thou should'st come to me,
But speak the words of comfort,
My spirit healed shall be.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: O Lord,
Thou art all holy,
The angels Thee adore;
How, then, ought I sincerely My wrongs and sins deplore!

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: But when Thou soon wilt enter My heart, my sinful heart,
Then heal me, be my shelter,
For Thou my Savior art.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: O Lord, how can I thank Thee For such a gift as this?
A gift which truly filleth My soul with heav'nly bliss!

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: I praise Thee,
I extol Thee,
I love Thee O my Sire,
Till once in joy and glory,
In heav'n I Thee admire.

title: O Lord, My God, I Thirst For You
author: Anthony Robertson

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: O Lord, my God,
I thirst for You,
I long to see your face,
Just as the hunted deer is stressed I falter in the race;
My heart cries out, my tears run down,
I am in deep distress, 'Where is your God?' men say to me,
They taunt me and oppress.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Lord, when will I be helped by You,
I struggle day and night?
O hear my prayer, enable me to stand in your great might;
I look back on those days gone by when,
Lord,
You were so near, when in your house with festive throng I praised your Name so dear.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: So why am I cast down,
O Lord, and why should I feel low?
You are my God, my Savior strong,
Your praise from me shall flow;
I think of all your works,
O Lord,
Your saving pow'r of old,
So when beset and overwhelmed,
I will your strength take hold.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Your lovingkindness fills my days,
Your song at night I sing,
And when my fears assail again to You I'll tight* ly cling;
My hope is fixed on God, my Rock,
His own He won't forget;
Be still my soul, my face will shine And I will praise Him yet.

title: O Lord My Soul Convicted (Here Lord My Soul Convicted)
author: James Maxwell

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: O Lord, my soul convicted stands Of breaking all Thy ten commands: And on me justly might'st Thou pour Thy wrath in one eternal show'r.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: But thanks to God, its loud alarms Have warn'd me of approaching harms;
And now,
O Lord, my wants I see,
Lost and undone,
I come to Thee.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: I know my fig leaf righteousness Can ne'er Thy broken law redress;
Yet in the gospel plan I see,
There's hope of pardon e'en for me.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: There,
I behold with wonder,
Lord!
That Christ hath to Thy law restor'd Those honors on th'a toning day,
Which guilty sinners took away.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Amazing wisdom, pow'r and love,
Dis play'd to rebels from above!
Do Thou,
O Lord, my faith increase To love and trust Thy plan of grace.

title: O Lord of Heav'n and Earth and Sea
author: Christopher Wordsworth

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: O Lord of Heav'n and earth and sea,
To Thee all praise and glory be;
How shall we show our love to Thee,
Who givest all?

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: The golden sunshine, ver* nal air,
Sweet flow'rs and fruits,
Thy love de* clare;
Where harvests ripen,
Thou art there,
Who givest all.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: For peaceful homes and health* ful days,
For all the blessings earth dis* plays,
We owe Thee thankfulness and praise,
Who givest all.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Thou didst not spare Thine on* ly Son,
But gav'st Him for a world un* done,
And freely, with that bless�d One,
Thou givest all.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Thou giv'st the Spirit's bless* �d dow'r,
Spir* it of life and love and pow'r,
And dost His sev'nfold graces show'r Up* on us all.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: For souls redeemed, for sins forgiv'n,
For means of grace and hopes of Heav'n,
Father, all praise to Thee be giv'n,
Who givest all.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: We lose what on ourselves we spend,
We have as treasure without end
Whatever, Lord, to Thee we lend,
Who givest all.

blocks.label: Verse 8
lines: To Thee, from Whom we all derive
Our life, our gifts, our power to give:
O may we ever with Thee live,
Who givest all.

title: O Lord We Praise Thee (May God be Praised Henceforth and Blest Forever or Let God Be Blest)
author: Martin Luther

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: O Lord, we praise Thee, bless Thee, and adore Thee,
In thanksgiving bow before Thee Thou with Thy body and Thy blood didst nourish Our weak souls that they may flou* rish: O Lord, have mer* cy!
May Thy body,
Lord, born of Mary,
That our sins and sor* rows did car* ry,
And Thy blood for us plead In all trial, fear, and need: O Lord, have mer* cy!

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Thy holy body into death was given,
Life to win for us in hea* ven.
No greater love than this to Thee could bind us;
May this feast thereof remind us!
O Lord, have mer* cy!
Lord,
Thy kindness did so constrain Thee That Thy blood should bless and sustain me.
All our debt Thou hast paid;
Peace with God once more is made: O Lord, have mer* cy.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: May God bestow on us His grace and favor To please Him with our beha* vior And live as brethren here in love and union Nor repent this blest Commun* ion!
O Lord, have mer* cy!
Let not Thy good Spirit forsake us;
Grant that heav'nly min* ded He make us;
Give Thy Church,
Lord, to see Days of peace and unity: O Lord, have mer* cy!

title: O Love, How Deep, How Broad, How High
author: unknown

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: O love, how deep, how broad, how high,
How pass* ing thought and fantasy,
That God, the Son of God, should take Our mortal form for mortals' sake!

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: He sent no angel to our race Of high* er or of lower place,
But wore the robe of human frame And He Himself, to this world came.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Nor willed He only to appear;
His plea* sure was to tarry here;
And God and Man with man would be The space of thirty years and three.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: For us baptized, for us He bore His ho* ly fast and hungered sore,
For us tempta* tions sharp He knew;
For us the tempter overthrew.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: For us He prayed;
for us He taught;
For us His dai* ly works He wrought;
By words and signs and actions thus Still seeking not Himself, but us.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: For us to wicked men betrayed,
Scourged, mocked, in crown of thorns arrayed,
For us He bore the cross's death,
For us at length gave up His breath.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: For us He rose from death again;
For us He went on high to reign;
For us He sent His Spirit here,
To guide, to strengthen, and to cheer.

blocks.label: Verse 8
lines: All honor, laud, and glory be,
O Jesus, virgin-born to Thee!
All glory, as is ever meet
To Father and to Paraclete.

title: O Sacred Head, Now Wounded
author: Bernard of Clairvaux

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: O sacred Head, now wounded, with grief and shame weighed down,
Now scornfully surrounded with thorns,
Thine on* ly crown;
O sac* red Head, what glory, what bliss till now was Thine!
Yet, though despised and gory,
I joy to call Thee mine.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: What Thou, my Lord, hast suffered, was all for sin* ners' gain;
Mine, mine was the transgression, but Thine the dead* ly pain.
Lo, here I fall, my Savior!
'Tis I deserve Thy place;
Look on me with Thy favor, vouchsafe to me Thy grace.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Men mock and taunt and jeer Thee,
Thou noble coun* tenance,
Though mighty worlds shall fear Thee and flee before Thy glance.
How art thou pale with anguish, with sore abuse and scorn!
How doth Thy visage languish that once was bright as morn!

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Now from Thy cheeks has vanished their color once so fair;
From Thy red lips is banished the splendor that was there.
Grim death, with cruel rigor, hath robbed Thee of Thy life;
Thus Thou hast lost Thy vigor,
Thy strength in this sad strife.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: My burden in Thy Passion,
Lord,
Thou hast borne for me,
For it was my transgression which brought this woe on Thee.
I cast me down before Thee, wrath were my rightful lot;
Have mer* cy,
I implore Thee;
Redeemer, spurn me not!

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: What language shall I borrow to thank Thee, dearest friend,
For this Thy dying sorrow, Thy pity without end?
O make me Thine forever, and should I fainting be,
Lord, let me never, never outlive my love to Thee.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: My Shepherd, now receive me; my Guardian, own me Thine.
Great blessings Thou didst give me, O source of gifts divine.
Thy lips have often fed me with words of truth and love;
Thy Spirit oft hath led me to heavenly joys above.

blocks.label: Verse 8
lines: Here I will stand beside Thee, from Thee I will not part;
O Savior, do not chide me! When breaks Thy loving heart,
When soul and body languish in death's cold, cruel grasp,
Then, in Thy deepest anguish, Thee in mine arms I'll clasp.

blocks.label: Verse 9
lines: The joy can never be spoken, above all joys beside,
When in Thy body broken I thus with safety hide.
O Lord of Life, desiring Thy glory now to see,
Beside Thy cross expiring, I'd breathe my soul to Thee.

blocks.label: Verse 10
lines: My Savior, be Thou near me when death is at my door;
Then let Thy presence cheer me, forsake me nevermore!
When soul and body languish, oh, leave me not alone,
But take away mine anguish by virtue of Thine own!

blocks.label: Verse 11
lines: Be Thou my consolation, my shield when I must die;
Remind me of Thy passion when my last hour draws nigh.
Mine eyes shall then behold Thee, upon Thy cross shall dwell,
My heart by faith enfolds Thee. Who dieth thus dies well.

title: O That The Lord Would Guide My Ways
author: Isaac Watts

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: O that the Lord would guide my ways To keep His statutes still!
O that my God would grant me grace To know and do His will!

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: O send Thy Spirit down to write Thy law upon my heart!
Nor let my tongue indulge deceit,
Nor act the liar's part.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: From vanity turn off mine eyes;
Let no corrupt design,
Nor covetous desires arise Within this soul of mine.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Order my footsteps by Thy Word,
And make my heart sincere;
Let sin have no dominion,
Lord,
But keep my conscience clear.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Assist my soul, too apt to stray,
A stricter watch to keep;
And should I e'er forget Thy way,
Restore Thy wand'ring sheep.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: Make me to walk in Thy commands, 'Tis a delightful road;
Nor let my head, or heart, or hands, Offend against my God.

title: O The Deep, Deep Love of Jesus
author: Samuel Trevor Francis

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: O the deep, deep love of Je* sus, vast, un* meas* ured, bound* less, free!
Rolling as a mighty o* cean in its full* ness ov* er me!
Under* neath me, all ar* ound me, is the current of Thy love Leading onward, leading home* ward to Thy glor* ious rest above!

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: O the deep, deep love of Je* sus, spread His praise from shore to shore!
How He loveth, ever lov* eth, changeth ne* ver, nev* ermore!
How He watches o'er His loved ones, died to call them all His own;
How for them He inter* ce* deth, watcheth o'er them from the throne!

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: O the deep, deep love of Je* sus, love of ev* ery love the best!
'Tis an ocean full of bless* ing, 'tis a ha* ven giv* ing rest!
O the deep, deep love of Jesus, 'tis a heav'n of heav'ns to me;
And it lifts me up to glo* ry, for it lifts me up to Thee!

title: O Trinity of Blessed Light (Thou Who Art Three in Unity)
author: Ambrose of Milan

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: O Trin* ity of bless* �d light,
O U* nity of prince* ly might,
The fiery sun now goes his way;
Shed Thou within our hearts a ray.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: To Thee our morning song of praise,
To Thee our evening prayer we raise;
O grant us with Thy saints on high To praise Thee through eter* ni* ty.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: All laud to God the Fa* ther be,
All praise, eternal Son, to Thee,
All glory, as is ev* er meet,
To God the holy Par* a* clete.

title: O Wondrous Type, O Vision Fair
author: Latin

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: O wondrous type!
O vision fair Of glo* ry that the Church may share,
Which Christ upon the mountain shows, where brighter than the sun He glows!

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: From age to age the tale declare,
How with the three di* sciples there,
Where Moses and El ijah meet,
The Lord holds converse high and sweet.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: The law and prophets there have place,
Two cho* sen wit* ness* es of grace;
The Father's voice from out the cloud proclaims His only Son aloud.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: With shining face and bright array,
Christ deigns to man* i* fest today What glory shall be theirs above who joy in God with perfect love.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: And faithful hearts are raised on high by this great vi* sion's mystery;
For which in joy* ful strains we raise the voice of prayer, the hymn of praise.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: O Father, with th'Eternal Son,
and Holy Spirit, ever One,
Vouchsafe to bring us by Thy grace
to see Thy glory face to face.

title: Of The Father's Love Begotten
author: Aurelius Clemens Prudentius

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Of the Father's love begot* ten Ere the worlds began to be,
He is Alpha and Ome* ga,
He the source, the end* ing He,
Of the things that are, that have been,
And that fu* ture years shall see,
Evermore and evermore!

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: At His Word they were crea* ted;
He commanded;
it was done: Heav'n and earth and depths of o* cean In their threefold or* der one;
All that grows beneath the shining Of the moon and burning sun,
Evermore and evermore!

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: He is found in human fash* ion,
Death and sorrow here to know,
That the race of Adam's child* ren,
Doomed by law to end* less woe,
May not henceforth die and perish In the dread* ful gulf below,
Evermore and evermore!

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Oh that birth forever bless* �d!
When the virgin, full of grace,
By the Holy Ghost conceiv* ing,
Bare the Savior of our race;
And the Babe, the world's Redeemer,
First re vealed His sacred face,
Evermore and evermore!

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: O ye heights of heav'n adore Him;
Angel hosts,
His prais* es sing;
Pow'rs, dominions, bow before Him, and extol our God and King: Let no tongue on earth be silent,
Ev* ery voice in concert ring,
Evermore and evermore!

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: He is here, Whom seers in old time Chanted of, while ages ran;
Whom the writings of the prophets Promised since the world began:
Then foretold, now manifested, to receive the praise of man,
Evermore and evermore!

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: Righteous Judge of souls departed, Righteous King of them that live,
On the Father's throne exalted None in might with Thee may strive;
Who at last in vengeance coming Sinners from Thy face shalt drive,
Evermore and evermore!

blocks.label: Verse 8
lines: Thee let old men, Thee let young men, Thee let choirs of infants sing;
Thee the matrons and the virgins, And the children answering:
Let their guileless songs re-echo, And the heart its music bring,
Evermore and evermore!

blocks.label: Verse 9
lines: Christ, to Thee with God the Father, And, O Holy Ghost, to Thee,
Hymn and chant with high thanksgiving, And unwearied praises be:
Honor, glory, and dominion, And eternal victory,
Evermore and evermore!

title: Oh, Blest the House
author: Christoph Karl Ludwig von Pfeil

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Oh blest the house, whate'er befall,
Where Jesus Christ is All in All;
Yea, if He were not dwelling there,
How poor and dark and void it were!

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Oh blest that house where faith ye find,
And all within have set their mind To trust their God and serve Him still,
And do in all His ho* ly will.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Blest, where their prayers shall daily rise As fragrant incense to the skies,
While in their lives the world is taught That forms without the heart are naught.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Blest, where the busy hands fulfil Their proper task with ready skill,
While through their different works ye see One spirit run of u* nity.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Blest such a house, it prospers well,
In peace and joy the parents dwell,
And in their children's lot is shown How richly God can bless His own.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: Then here will I and mine to-day
A solemn covenant make, and say,--
Though all the world forsake Thy Word,
I and my house will serve the Lord.

title: On Jordan's Bank the Baptist's Cry
author: Charles Coffin

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: On Jordan's bank the Baptist's cry Announces that the Lord is nigh;
Come, then, and hearken, for he brings Glad tidings from the King of kings!

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Then cleansed be every breast from sin;
Make straight the way for God within;
Prepare we in our hearts a home,
Where such a mighty Guest may come.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: For Thou art our Salvation,
Lord,
Our Refuge, and our great Reward.
Without Thy grace our souls must fade And wither like a flow'r decayed.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Stretch forth Thine hand, to heal our sore,
And make us rise and fall no more;
Once more upon Thy people shine,
And fill the world with love divine.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: To Him Who left the throne of Heav'n To save man kind, all praise be giv'n;
Like praise be to the Father done,
And Holy Spirit,
Three in One.

title: On What Has Now Been Sown
author: John Newton

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: On what has now been sown Thy blessing,
Lord, bestow;
The pow'r is Thine alone To make it spring and grow.
Do Thou in grace the harvest raise,
And Thou alone shalt have the praise.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: To Thee our wants are known,
From Thee are all our pow'rs;
Accept what is Thine own And pardon what is ours.
Our praises,
Lord, and prayers receive And to Thy Word a blessing give.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Oh, grant that each of us Now met before Thee here May meet together thus When Thou and Thine appear And follow Thee to Heav'n, our home.
E'en so,
Amen,
Lord Jesus, come!

title: One Thing's Needful
author: Johann Heinrich Schr�der

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: One thing's needful: then,
Lord Jesus,
Keep this one thing in my mind;
All beside, though first it please us,
Soon a grievous yoke we find: Be* neath it the heart is still fretting and striving,
No true, lasting happiness ever deriving.
The gain of this one thing all loss can requite And teach me in all things to find true delight.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Soul, wilt thou this one thing find thee?
Seek not midst created things;
What is earthly, leave behind thee, over nature stretch thy wings;
For where God and man both in One are united,
With God's perfect fullness the heart is delighted;
There, there is the worthiest lot and the best,
My One and my All, and my Joy, and my Rest.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: How were Mary's thoughts devoted,
Her eternal joy to find,
As intent each word she noted,
At her Savior's feet reclined: How kindled her heart, how de* vout was its feeling,
While hearing the lessons that Christ was revealing;
For Jesus all earthly con* cerns she forgot,
And all was repaid in that one happy lot.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Thus my longings, heav'nward tending,
Jesus, rest alone on Thee;
Help me, thus on Thee depending,
Savior!
come and dwell in me: Al* though all the world should for* sake and forget Thee,
In love I will follow Thee, ne'er will I quit Thee;
For Jesus, both Spirit and life is Thy Word,
And is there a joy which Thou dost not afford?

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Wisdom's highest noblest treasure,
Jesus, lies conceal'd in Thee;
Grant that this may still the measure Of my will and actions be: Hu* mility there and sim* plicity reigning,
My steps shall in wisdom for ever be training;
Oh!
if I of Christ have this knowledge divine,
The fullness of heavenly wisdom is mine.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: Christ, Thou art the sole oblation
That I'll bring before my God;
In his sight I've acceptation
Only through Thy streaming blood:
Immaculate righteousness now I've acquired,
Since Thou on the tree of the cross hast expired;
The robe of salvation for ever is mine,
In this shall my faith through eternity shine.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: Let my soul, in full exemption,
Wake up in Thy likeness now;
Thou art made to me redemption,
My sanctification Thou.
Whatever I need for my Journey to Heaven
In Thee, I my Savior, is unto me given.
Oh! let me all perishing pleasures forgo,
And Thy life, O Jesus! alone let me know.

blocks.label: Verse 8
lines: Where should else my hopes be centered?
Grace o'erwhelms me with its flood;
Thou, my Savior, once hast enter'd
Holiest heaven through Thy blood:
Eternal redemption for sinners there finding,
From hell's dark dominion my spirit unbinding,
To me perfect freedom Thy entrance has brought,
And childlike to cry, "Abba, Father," I'm taught.

blocks.label: Verse 9
lines: Christ Himself, my Shepherd, feeds me,
Peace and joy my spirit fill;
In a pasture green He leads me
Forth beside the waters still:
Oh! naught to my soul is so sweet and reviving,
As thus unto Jesus alone to be living;
True happiness this, and this only supplies,
Through faith on my Savior to fasten my eyes.

blocks.label: Verse 10
lines: Therefore, Jesus, my Salvation,
Thou my One, my All shalt be;
Prove my fix'd determination,
Root out all hypocrisy:
Look well if on sin's slippery paths I am hasting,
And lead me, O Lord, in the way everlasting;
This one thing is needful, all others are vain,
I count all but loss that I Christ may obtain.

title: Open Now Thy Gates of Beauty
author: Benjamin Schmolck

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Open now thy gates of beauty,
Zion, let me enter there,
Where my soul in joyful duty Waits for Him Who answers prayer.
Oh, how bless�d is this place,
Filled with solace, light and grace!

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Lord, my God,
I come before Thee,
Come Thou also unto me;
Where we find Thee and adore Thee,
There a heav'n on earth must be.
To my heart, oh, enter Thou,
Let it be Thy temple now!

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Here Thy praise is gladly chanted,
Here Thy seed is duly sown;
Let my soul, where it is planted,
Bring forth precious sheaves alone,
So that all I hear may be Fruitful unto life in me.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Thou my faith increase and quicken,
Let me keep Thy gift divine,
Howsoe'er temptations thicken;
May Thy Word still o'er me shine As my guiding star through life,
As my comfort in my strife.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Speak,
O God, and I will hear Thee,
Let Thy will be done indeed;
May I undisturbed draw near Thee While Thou dost Thy people feed.
Here of life the fountain flows,
Here is balm for all our woes.

title: Our Father Thou in Heaven Above (Our Father, Who from Heaven Above or Our Father in the Heaven Who Art)
author: Martin Luther

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Our Father,
Thou in heav'n above,
Who biddest us to dwell in love,
As brethren of one family,
To cry in ev'ry need to Thee,
Teach us no thoughtless word to say,
But from our inmost heart to pray.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Thy name be hallowed.
Help us,
Lord,
In purity to keep Thy Word,
That to the glory of Thy Name We walk before Thee free from blame.
Let no false doctrine us pervert;
All poor, deluded souls convert.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Thy kingdom come.
Thine let it be In time and in eternity.
Let Thy good Spirit e'er be nigh Our hearts with graces to supply.
Break Satan's pow'r, defeat his rage;
Preserve Thy Church from age to age.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Thy gracious will on earth be done As 'tis in heav'n before Thy throne;
Obedience in our weal and woe And patience in all grief bestow.
Curb flesh and blood and ev'ry ill That sets itself against Thy will.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Give us this day our daily bread And let us all be clothed and fed.
From war and strife be our Defense,
From famine and from pestilence,
That we may live in godly peace,
Free from all care and avarice.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: Forgive our sins, Lord, we implore,
Remove from us their burden sore,
As we their trespasses forgive
Who by offenses us do grieve.
Thus let us dwell in charity
And serve our brother willingly.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: Into temptation lead us not.
When evil foes against us plot
And vex our souls on every hand,
Oh, give us strength that we may stand
Firm in the faith, a well-armed host,
Through comfort of the Holy Ghost!

blocks.label: Verse 8
lines: From evil, Lord, deliver us;
The times and days are perilous.
Redeem us from eternal death,
And when we yield our dying breath,
Console us, grant us calm release,
And take our souls to Thee in peace.

blocks.label: Verse 9
lines: Amen, that is, So shall it be.
Confirm our faith and hope in Thee
That we may doubt not, but believe
What here we ask we shall receive.
Thus in Thy name and at Thy word
We say: Amen. Oh, hear us, Lord! Amen.

title: Our God, Our Help In Ages Past
author: Isaac Watts

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Our God, our help in ages past,
Our hope for years to come,
Our shelter from the stormy blast,
And our eternal home.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Under the shadow of Thy throne Thy saints have dwelt secure;
Sufficient is Thine arm alone,
And our defense is sure.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Before the hills in order stood,
Or earth received her frame,
From everlasting Thou art God,
To endless years the same.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Thy Word commands our flesh to dust, 'Return, ye sons of men:' All nations rose from earth at first,
And turn to earth again.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: A thousand ages in Thy sight Are like an evening gone;
Short as the watch that ends the night Before the rising sun.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: The busy tribes of flesh and blood,
With all their lives and cares,
Are carried downwards by the flood,
And lost in following years.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: Time, like an ever rolling stream,
Bears all its sons away;
They fly, forgotten, as a dream
Dies at the opening day.

blocks.label: Verse 8
lines: Like flowery fields the nations stand
Pleased with the morning light;
The flowers beneath the mower's hand
Lie withering ere 'tis night.

blocks.label: Verse 9
lines: Our God, our help in ages past,
Our hope for years to come,
Be Thou our guard while troubles last,
And our eternal home.

title: Out of the Deep I Cry to Thee (From Depths of Woe I Cry to Thee)
author: Martin Luther

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Out of the deep I cry to Thee;
O Lord God, hear my cry* ing: Incline Thy gracious ear to me,
With prayer to Thee apply* ing.
For if Thou fix Thy search* ing eye On all sin and iniquity,
Who,
Lord, can stand before Thee?

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: But love and grace with Thee prevail,
O God, our sins forgiv* ing;
The holiest deeds can naught avail Of all before Thee liv* ing.
Before Thee none can boast him clear;
Therefore must each Thy judgment fear,
And live on Thy compas* sion.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: For this, my hope in God shall rest,
Naught building on my mer* it;
My heart confides, of Him possest,
His goodness stays my spi* rit.
His precious word assur* eth me;
My solace, my sure Rock is he,
Whereon my soul abid* eth.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: And though I wait the livelong night And till the morn return* eth,
My heart undoubting trusts His might Nor in impa* tience mourn* eth.
Born of His Spirit,
Is* rael In the right Way thus fareth well,
And on his God repos* eth

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: What though our sins are manifold?
Supreme His mer* cy reign* eth;
No limit can His hand withhold,
Where evil most obtain* eth.
He the good Shepherd is alone,
Who Israel will redeem and own,
Forgiving all transgres* sion.

title: Over Kidron Jesus Treadeth (Over Kedron Jesus Treadeth or Over Cedron Jesus Treadeth)
author: Thomas Hansen Kingo

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Over Kidron Jesus treadeth To His passion for us all;
Every human eye be weeping,
Tears of bitter grief let fall!
Round His Spirit flock the foes,
Place their shafts and bend their bows,
Aiming at the Savior solely,
While the world forsakes Him wholly.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: David once, with heart afflicted,
Crossed the Kidron's narrow strand,
Clouds of gloom and grief about him When an exile from his land.
But,
O Jesus, blacker now Bends the cloud above Thy brow,
Hasting to death's dreary portals For the shame and sin of mortals.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: See how, anguish struck,
He falleth Prostrate, and with struggling breath,
Three times on His God He calleth,
Praying that the bitter death And the cup of doom may go,
Still He cries, in all His woe: "Not My will, but Thine,
O Father!" And the angels round Him gather.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: See how, in that hour of darkness,
Battling with the evil pow'r,
Agonies untold assail Him,
On His soul the arrows show'r;
All the garden flow'rs are wet With the drops of bloody sweat,
From His anguished frame distillingWorld's redemption thus ful* filling!

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: But,
O flow'rs, so sadly watered By this pure and precious dew,
In some blessed hour your blossoms 'Neath the olive shadows grew!
Eden's garden did not bear Aught that can with you compare,
For the blood, thus freely given,
Makes my soul the heir of heaven.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: When as flow'rs themselves I wither, When I droop and fade like grass,
When the life-streams through my pulses Dull and ever duller pass,
When at last they cease to roll, Then, to cheer my sinking soul,
Grace of Jesus, be Thou given- Source of triumph! pledge of heaven!

title: Pass Me Not, O Gentle Savior
author: Fanny Jane Crosby

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Pass me not,
O gentle Savior,
Hear my humble cry;
Trusting only in Thy merit,
Would I seek Thy face;
While on others Thou art calling,
Do not pass me by.
Heal my wounded, broken spirit,
Save me by Thy grace.
Savior,
Sa* vior,
Hear my humble cry;

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Let me at Thy throne of mercy Find a sweet relief,
Thou the Spring of all my comfort,
More than life to me,
Kneeling there in deep contrition;
Help my unbelief.
Whom have I on earth beside Thee?
Whom in Heav'n but Thee?
While on others Thou art calling,
Do not pass me by.

title: (Doxology; see also 'Awake, My Soul, And With The Sun')
author: Thomas Ken

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Praise God, from Whom all blessings flow;
Praise Him, all creatures here below;
Praise Him above, ye heav'nly host;
Praise Father,
Son, and Holy Ghost.

title: Praise My Soul The King Of Heaven
author: Henry F. Lyte

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Praise, my soul, the King of heaven;
To His feet thy tribute bring.
Ransomed, healed, restored, forgiven,
Evermore His praises sing: Alleluia!
Alleluia!
Praise the everlasting King.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Praise Him for His grace and favor To our fathers in distress.
Praise Him still the same as ever,
Slow to chide, and swift to bless.
Alleluia!
Alleluia!
Glorious in His faithfulness.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Father like He tends and spares us;
Well our feeble frame He knows.
In His hands He gently bears us,
Rescues us from all our foes.
Alleluia!
Alleluia!
Widely yet His mercy flows.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Frail as summer's flower we flourish,
Blows the wind and it is gone;
But while mortals rise and perish Our God lives unchanging on,
Praise Him,
Praise Him,
Hallelujah Praise the High Eternal One!

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Angels, help us to adore Him;
Ye behold Him face to face;
Sun and moon, bow down before Him,
Dwellers all in time and space.
Alleluia!
Alleluia!
Praise with us the God of grace.

title: Praise The Lord, Ye Heavens Adore Him
author: Edward Osler

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Praise the Lord, ye heav'ns, adore Him;
Praise Him, angels in the height.
Sun and moon, rejoice before Him;
Praise Him, all ye stars of light.
Praise the Lord, for He hath spo* ken;
Worlds His mighty voice o* beyed.
Laws which never shall be bro* ken For their gui* dance He hath made.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Praise the Lord, for He is glor* ious;
Never shall His promise fail.
God hath made His saints victor* ious;
Sin and death shall not pre* vail.
Praise the God of our salva* tion;
Hosts on high,
His pow'r pro* claim.
Heav'n and earth and all crea* tion,
Laud and mag* ni* fy His name.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Worship, honor, glory, bless* ing,
Lord, we offer unto Thee.
Young and old,
Thy praise express* ing,
In glad homage bend the knee.
All the saints in Heav'n adore Thee;
We would bow before Thy throne.
As Thine angels serve before Thee,
So on earth Thy will be done.

title: Praise To The Lord, The Almighty
author: Joachim Neander

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Praise to the Lord, the Almighty, the King of creation!
O my soul, praise Him, for He is thy health and salvation!
All ye who hear, now to His temple draw near;
Praise Him in glad adoration.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Praise to the Lord,
Who o'er all things so wondrously reigneth,
Shelters thee under His wings, yea, so gently sustaineth!
Hast thou not seen how thy desires have been Granted in what He ordaineth

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Praise to the Lord,
Who hath fearfully, wondrously, made thee;
Health hath vouchsafed and, when heedlessly falling, hath stayed thee.
What need or grief ever hath failed of relief?
Wings of His mercy did shade thee.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Praise to the Lord,
Who doth prosper thy work and defend thee;
Surely His goodness and mercy here daily attend thee.
Ponder anew what the Almighty can do,
If with His love He befriend thee.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Praise to the Lord,
Who, when tempests their warfare are waging,
Who, when the elements madly around thee are raging,
Biddeth them cease, turneth their fury to peace,
Whirlwinds and waters assuaging.

title: Rejoice, My Heart, Be Glad and Sing (O Lord I Sing with Lips and Heart)
author: Paul Gerhardt

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Rejoice, my heart, be glad and sing,
A cheerful trust maintain;
For God, the Source of everything,
Thy Portion shall remain.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: He is thy Treasure,
He thy Joy,
Thy Life and Light and Lord,
Thy Counselor when doubts annoy,
Thy Shield and great Reward.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Why spend the day in blank despair,
In restless thought the night?
On thy Creator cast thy care;
He makes thy burdens light.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Did not His love and truth and pow'r Watch o'er thy childhood day?
Has He not oft in threat'ning hour Turned dreaded ills away?

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: His wisdom never plans in vain,
Ne'er falters or mistakes;
All that His counsels did ordain A happy ending makes.

title: Rejoice, O Pilgrim Throng (Rejoice Ye Pure in Heart)
author: Edward Hayes Plumptre

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Rejoice,
O pilgrim throng!
Rejoice, give thanks, and sing;
Your festal banner wave on high,
The cross of Christ your King.
Rejoice, rejoice, rejoice,
Give thanks and sing.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: With all the angel choirs,
With all the saints on earth,
Pour out the strains of joy and bliss,
True rapture, noblest mirth.
Re* joice, re* joice, rejoice,
Give thanks and sing.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: With voice as full and strong As ocean's surging praise,
Send forth the hymns our fa* thers loved,
The psalms of ancient days.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Still lift your standard high,
Still march in firm array,
As warriors through the dark* ness toil,
Till dawns the golden day.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Yes, on through life's long path,
Still chanting as ye go;
From youth to age, by night and day,
In gladness and in woe.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: Yes onward, onward still With hymn, and chant and song,
Through gate, and porch and columned aisle, The hallowed pathways throng.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: At last the march shall end; The wearied ones shall rest;
The pilgrims find their Father's house, Jerusalem the bless'd.

blocks.label: Verse 8
lines: Then on, ye pure in heart! Rejoice, give thanks and sing!
Your festal banner wave on high, The cross of Christ your King.

title: Rescue the Perishing
author: Fanny Jane Crosby

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Rescue the perishing, care for the dying,
Snatch them in pity from sin and the grave;
Weep o'er the erring one, lift up the fallen,
Tell them of Jesus, the mighty to save.
Rescue the perishing,

blocks.label: Refrain
lines: care for the dying,
Jesus is merciful,
Jesus will save.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Though they are slighting Him, still He is waiting,
Waiting the penitent child to receive;
Plead with them earnestly, plead with them gently;
He will forgive they should only believe.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Down in the human heart, crushed by the tempter,
Feelings lie buried that grace can restore;
Touched by a loving heart, wakened by kindness,
Chords that were broken will vibrate once more.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Rescue the perishing, duty demands it;
Strength for thy labor the Lord will provide;
Back to the narrow way patiently win them;
Tell the poor wand'rer a Savior has died.

title: Rock of Ages
author: Augustus Montague Toplady

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Rock of Ages, cleft for me,
Let me hide myself in Thee;
Let the water and the blood,
From Thy wounded side which flowed,
Be of sin the double cure;
Save from wrath and make me pure.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Not the labor of my hands Can fulfill Thy law's demands;
Could my zeal no respite know,
Could my tears forever flow,
All for sin could not atone;
Thou must save, and Thou alone.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Nothing in my hand I bring,
Simply to the cross I cling;
Naked, come to Thee for dress;
Helpless look to Thee for grace;
Foul,
I to the fountain fly;
Wash me,
Savior, or I die.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: While I draw this fleeting breath,
When mine eyes shall close in death,
When I soar to worlds unknown,
See Thee on Thy judgment throne,
Rock of Ages, cleft for me,
Let me hide myself in Thee.

title: Salvation Unto Us Has Come (To Us Salvation Now Is Come)
author: Paul Speratus

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Salvation unto us has come By God's free grace and fa* vor;
Good works cannot avert our doom,
They help and save us ne* ver.
Faith looks to Jesus Christ alone,
Who did for all the world atone;
He is our one Redeem* er.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: What God did in His law demand And none to Him could ren* der Caused wrath and woe on every hand For man, the vile offend* er.
Our flesh has not those pure desires The spirit of the Law requires,
And lost is our condi* tion.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: It was a false, misleading dream That God His Law had gi* ven So sinners could themselves redeem And by their works gain Hea* ven.
The Law is but a mirror bright To bring the inbred sin to light That lurks within our na* ture.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: From sin our flesh could not abstain Sin held its sway uncea* sing;
The task was useless and in vain,
Our guilt was e'er increa* sing.
None can remove sin's poisoned dart Or purify our guileful heart?
So deep is our corru* ption.

title: Savior, Like A Shepherd Lead Us
author: Dorothy Ann Thrupp

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Savior, like a shepherd lead us, much we need Thy tender care;
In Thy pleasant pastures feed us, for our use Thy folds prepare.
Bless�d Jesus, bless�d Jesus!
Thou hast bought us,
Thine we are.
Bless�d Jesus, bless�d Jesus!
Thou hast bought us,
Thine we are.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: We are Thine,
Thou dost befriend us, be the guardian of our way;
Keep Thy flock, from sin defend us, seek us when we go astray.
Bless�d Jesus, bless�d Jesus!
Hear,
O hear us when we pray.
Bless�d Jesus, bless�d Jesus!
Hear,
O hear us when we pray.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Thou hast promised to receive us, poor and sinful though we be;
Thou hast mercy to relieve us, grace to cleanse and pow'r to free.
Bless�d Jesus, bless�d Jesus!
We will early turn to Thee.
Bless�d Jesus, bless�d Jesus!
We will early turn to Thee.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Early let us seek Thy fa* vor, early let us do Thy will;
Bless�d Lord and only Sa* vior, with Thy love our bosoms fill.
Bless�d Jesus, bless�d Jesus!
Thou hast loved us, love us still.
Bless�d Jesus, bless�d Jesus!
Thou hast loved us, love us still.

title: Savior Of The Nations Come
author: Ambrose of Milan

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Savior of the na* tions, come;
Virgin's Son, here make Thy home!
Marvel now,
O heav'n and earth,
That the Lord chose such a birth.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Not by human flesh and blood;
By the Spirit of our God Was the Word of God made flesh,
Woman's offspring, pure and fresh.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Wondrous birth!
O won* drous Child Of the virgin undefiled!
Though by all the world dis* owned,
Still to be in heaven enthroned.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: From the Father forth He came And returneth to the same,
Captive leading death and hell High the song of tri* umph swell!

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Thou, the Father's on* ly Son,
Hast o'er sin the vict'ry won.
Boundless shall Thy kingdom be;
When shall we its glo* ries see?

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: Brightly doth Thy manger shine,
Glorious is its light divine.
Let not sin o'ercloud this light;
Ever be our faith thus bright.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: Praise to God the Father sing,
Praise to God the Son, our King,
Praise to God the Spirit be
Ever and eternally.

title: Savior When In Dust To Thee
author: Robert Grant

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Savior, when in dust to Thee Low we bow th'ador* ing knee,
When, re* pent* ant, to the skies Scarce we lift our weeping eyes,
O by all the pains and woes Suffered once for man be* low,
Bending from Thy throne on high,
Hear our pen* itential cry!

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: By Thy help* less infant years,
By Thy life of want and tears,
By Thy days of sore distress In the savage wilderness,
By the dread mysterious hour Of th'insulting tempter's pow'r,
Turn,
O turn a fav'ring eye,
Hear our pen* itential cry!

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: By the sac* red griefs that wept O'er the grave where La* z'rus slept,
By the bod* ing tears that flowed Over Salem's loved abode,
By the anguished sigh that told Treachery lurked within Thy fold,
From Thy seat above the sky,
Hear our pen* itential cry!

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: By Thine hour of dire despair,
By Thine agony of prayer,
By the cross, the nail, the thorn,
Piercing spear, and torturing scorn,
By the gloom that veiled the skies O'er the dreadful sacri* fice,
Listen to our humble cry,
Hear our pen* itential cry!

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: By Thy deep expiring groan,
By the sad sepul* chral stone,
By the vault whose dark abode Held in vain the rising God,
O from earth to heaven re* stored,
Mighty, reascended Lord,
Listen, listen to the sigh Of our pen* itential cry!

title: Savior, Who Thy Flock Art Feeding
author: William Augustus M�hlenberg

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Savior, who Thy flock art feeding With the Shepherd's kindest care,
All the feeble gently leading,
While the lambs Thy bosom share.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Now, these little ones receiving,
Fold them in Thy gracious arm;
There, we know,
Thy Word be* lieving,
Only there secure from harm.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Never, from Thy pasture roving,
Let them be the lion's prey;
Let Thy tender* ness, so loving,
Keep them through life's dang'rous way.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Then within Thy fold eternal Let them find a resting place,
Feed in pastures ever vernal,
Drink the rivers of Thy grace.

title: See Amid the Winter's Snow
author: Edward Caswall

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: See amid the winter's snow,
Born for us on earth below,
See, the gentle Lamb appears,
Promised from eternal years.
Hail that ever bless�d morn,
Hail redemption's happy dawn,

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Lo, within a manger lies He Who built the starry skies;
He Who, thron�d in height sublime,
Sits amid the cherubim.
Sing through all Jerusalem: Christ is born in Bethlehem.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Say, you holy shepherds, say,
Tell your joyful news today.
Why have you now left your sheep On the lonely mountain steep?

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: "As we watched at dead of night,
Lo, we saw a wondrous light;
Angels singing 'Peace on earth' Told us of the Savior's birth."

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Sacred Infant, all divine,
What a tender love was Thine,
Thus to come from highest bliss Down to such a world as this.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: Teach, O teach us, holy Child,
By Thy face so meek and mild,
Teach us to resemble Thee,
In Thy sweet humility.

title: See, The Lord Ascends In Triumph (See, the Conqueror Mounts in Triumph)
author: Christopher Wordsworth

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: See, the Lord ascends in triumph;
see the King in royal state,
Riding on the clouds,
His chariot,
To His heav'nly palace gate.
Hark!
the choirs of angel voices Joyful al* leluias sing,
And the portals high are lifted To receive their heav'nly King.
Holy Ghost,
Illuminator, shed Thy beams upon our eyes,
Help us to look up with Stephen, and to see beyond the skies,
Where the Son of Man in glory Standing is at God's right hand,
Beck'ning on His martyr army, succoring His faith* ful band.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Who is this that comes in glory, with the trump of jubilee?
Lord of battles,
God of armies,
He has gained the victory.
He Who on the cross did suffer,
He who from the grave arose,
He has vanquished sin and Satan,
He by death has spoiled His foes.
See Him,
Who is gone before us,
Heav'nly mansions to prepare,
See Him, who is ever pleading For us with prevail* ing prayer,
See Him, who with sound of trumpet, and with His angel* ic train,
Summoning the world to judgment, on the clouds will come again.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: While He lifts His hands in blessing,
He is parted from His friends While their eager eyes behold Him,
He upon the cloud ascends;
He Who walked with God and pleased Him, preaching truth and doom to come,
He, our Enoch, is translated to His everlasting home.
Raise us up from earth to Heaven, give us wings of faith and love,
Gales of holy aspirations wafting us to realms above;
That, with hearts and minds uplifted, we with Christ our Lord may dwell,
Where He sits enthroned in glory in His heav'nly Cit* adel.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Now our heav'nly Aaron enters, with His blood, with* in the veil;
Joshua now is come to Canaan, and the kings before Him quail;
Now He plants the tribes of Israel in their pro* mised resting place;
Now our great Elijah offers double portion of His grace.
So at last, when He appeareth, we from out our graves may spring,
With our youth renewed like eagles, flocking round our Heav'n* ly King.
Caught up on the clouds of Heaven, and may meet Him in the air,
Rise to realms where He is reigning, and may reign for ev* er there.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: He has raised our human nature in the clouds to God's right hand;
There we sit in heav'nly places, there with Him in glory stand: Jesus reigns, adored by angels;
man with God is on the throne;
Mighty Lord, in Thine ascension we by faith behold our own.
Glory be to God the Father,
Glory be to God the Son,
Dying, ris'n, ascending for us, who the heav'nly realm has won;
Glory to the Holy Spirit,
To One God in Per* sons Three;
Glory both in earth and Heaven, glory, endless glo* ry, be.

title: Silent Night
author: Josef Mohr

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Si* lent night, ho* ly night,
All is calm, all is bright Round yon vir* gin mother and Child.
Holy Infant, so tender and mild,
Sleep in heavenly peace,
Sleep in heavenly peace.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Si* lent night, ho* ly night,
Shepherds quake at the sight;
Glories stream from heaven afar,
Heavenly hosts sing Allelu ia!
Christ the Savior is born,
Christ the Savior is born!

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Si* lent night, ho* ly night,
Son of God, love's pure light;
Radiant beams from Thy holy face With the dawn of redeem* ing grace,
Jesus,
Lord, at Thy birth,
Je* sus,
Lord, at Thy birth.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Si* lent night, ho* ly night Wondrous star, lend thy light;
With the an* gels let us sing,
Allelu* ia to our King;
Christ the Savior is born,
Christ the Savior is born!

title: Sing, O Sing, This Blessed Morn
author: Christopher Wordsworth

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Sing,
O sing, this blessed morn,
Unto us a Child is born,
Unto us a Son is giv'n,
God Himself comes down from Heav'n.

blocks.label: Refrain
lines: Sing,
O sing, this blessed morn,
Jesus Christ today is born.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Jesus Christ, the King of kings,
Maker of all worldly things,
Now descends from Heav'n to Earth,
To re-store us by His birth;

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: God of God, and Light of Light,
Comes with mercies infinite;
Joining in a wondrous plan Heav'n to earth and God to Man;

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: God with us,
Emmanuel,
Deigns for ever now to dwell;
He on Adam's fallen race Sheds the fullness of His Grace;

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Truth and Mercy show their face,
And with loving kiss embrace;
Righteousness looks down from Heav'n,
God is pleased and Man forgiv'n;

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: God comes down that man may rise, Lifted far above the skies
He is Son of Man, that we Sons of God in Him may be;

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: Human flesh is now become Christ's abode, the Godhead's home;
Royal Palace, sacred shrine For the Majesty Divine;

blocks.label: Verse 8
lines: Now we rise, from prison free; On we march to victory,
Joyful banners are unfurled; 'Tis the Birthday of the World;

blocks.label: Verse 9
lines: Now behold the rising Sun Hath His glorious race begun;
Now the Bridegroom from above Weds the Bride, with heavenly love;

blocks.label: Verse 10
lines: O renew us, Lord, we pray, With Thy Spirit day by day;
That we ever one may be With the Father, and with Thee;

blocks.label: Verse 11
lines: Sing, O sing this blessed Morn, Jesus Christ to-day is born;
Glory to the Father give, Praise the Son in whom we live;
Glory to the Spirit be, Godhead One, and Persons Three.

title: Songs of Thankfulness and Praise
author: Christopher Wordsworth

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Songs of thankfulness and praise,
Jesus,
Lord, to Thee we raise,
Manifested by the star To the sages from afar;
Branch of royal David's stem In Thy birth at Bethlehem;
Anthems be to Thee addressed,
God in man made manifest.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Manifest at Jordan's stream,
Prophet,
Priest, and King supreme;
And at Cana, wedding guest,
In Thy Godhead manifest;
Manifest in pow'r divine,
Changing water into wine;
Anthems be to Thee addressed,
God in man made manifest.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Manifest in making whole Palsied limbs and fainting soul;
Manifest in valiant fight,
Quelling all the devil's might;
Manifest in gracious will,
Ever bringing good from ill;
Anthems be to Thee addressed,
God in man made manifest.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Sun and moon shall darkened be,
Stars shall fall, the heav'ns shall flee,
Christ will then like lightning shine,
All will see His glorious sign: All will then the trumpet hear;
All will see the Judge appear;
Thou by all wilt be confessed,
God in man made manifest.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Grant us grace to see Thee,
Lord,
Mirrored in Thy holy Word;
May we imitate Thee now,
And be pure, as pure art Thou;
That we like to Thee may be At Thy great Epiphany;
And may praise Thee, ever blest,
God in man made manifest.

title: Souls of Men! Why Will Ye Scatter (There's a Wideness in God's Mercy)
author: Frederick William Faber

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Souls of men!
why will ye scatter Like a crowd of fright* ened sheep?
Foolish hearts!
why will ye wander From a love so true and deep?
Was there ever kinder shepherd Half so gentle, half so sweet,
As the Savior who would have us Come and gather round His feet?

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: It is God: His love looks mighty,
But is mighti'r than it seems;
'Tis our Father: and His fondness Goes far out be* yond our dreams.
There's a wideness in God's mercy,
Like the wideness of the sea;
There's a kindness in His justice,
Which is more than lib* er* ty.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: There is no place where earth's sorrows Are more felt than up in Heav'n;
There is no place where earth's failings Have such wondrous judg* ment giv'n.
There is welcome for the sinner,
Grace poured out as in a flood There is mercy with the Savior;
There is healing in His blood.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: There is grace enough for thousands Of new worlds as great as this;
There is room for fresh cre* ations In that upper home of bliss.
For the love of God is broader Than the measure of man's mind;
And the heart of the E* ternal Is most wonder* ful* ly kind.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: There is plentiful re* demption In Christ's blood that has been shed;
There is joy for all the members In the sorrows of the Head.
Not just all we owe to Jesus;
It is something more than all;
Greater good because of evil,
Larger mercy through the fall.

title: Stricken, Smitten, and Afflicted
author: Thomas Kelly

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Stricken, smitten, and afflicted,
See Him dying on the tree!
'Tis the Christ by man rejected;
Yes, my soul, 'tis He, 'tis He!
'Tis the long expected prophet,
David's Son, yet David's Lord;
Proofs I see sufficient of it: 'Tis a true and faithful Word.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Tell me, ye who hear Him groaning,
Was there ever grief like His?
Friends through fear His cause disowning,
Foes insulting his distress: Many hands were raised to wound Him,
None would interpose to save;
But the deepest stroke that pierced Him Was the stroke that Justice gave.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Ye who think of sin but lightly,
Nor suppose the evil great,
Here may view its nature rightly,
Here its guilt may estimate.
Mark the Sacrifice appointed!
See Who bears the awful load!
'Tis the Word, the Lord's Anointed,
Son of Man, and Son of God.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Here we have a firm foundation,
Here the refuge of the lost.
Christ the Rock of our salvation,
Christ the Name of which we boast.
Lamb of God for sinners wounded!
Sacrifice to cancel guilt!
None shall ever be confounded Who on Him their hope have built.

title: Take My Life And Let It Be
author: Frances Ridley Havergal

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Take my life, and let it be consecra* ted,
Lord, to Thee.
Take my mo* ments and my days;
let them flow in ceaseless praise.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Take my hands, and let them move at the im* pulse of Thy love.
Take my feet, and let them be swift and beau* tiful for Thee.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Take my voice, and let me sing always, on* ly, for my King.
Take my lips, and let them be filled with mess* ages from Thee.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Take my silver and my gold;
not a mite would I with* hold.
Take my in* tellect, and use every pow'r as Thou shalt choose.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Take my will, and make it Thine;
it shall be no longer mine.
Take my heart, it is Thine own;
it shall be Thy royal throne.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: Take my love, my Lord, I pour at Thy feet its treasure store.
Take myself, and I will be ever, only, all for Thee.

title: Take Thou My Hand and Lead Me (O Take My Hand, Dear Father or Lord Take My Hand and Lead Me)
author: Julie Katharina von Hausmann

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Take Thou my hand, and lead me o'er life's rough way, with Heav'nly Manna feed me from day to day.
Alone my footsteps fal* ter and straggle wide,
Lord who my life canst alter be Thou my guide.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Take Thou my heart and hide it in folds of grace Though pain or woe betide it to know Thy face Draw,
Lord, of Thy good plea* sure Thy child to Thee,
And grant me faith's full measure though naught I see.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Though oft I think Thou hidest Thy wondrous might,
Still to my goal Thou guidest me through dark night,
Take, then, my hands and lead me till life is o'er,
With heav'nly manna feed me forev* ermore.

title: 'Take Up Thy Cross', the Savior Said
author: Charles William Everest

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: "Take up thy cross," the Savior said, "If thou wouldst My disciple be;
Deny thyself, the world forsake,
And humbly follow after Me."

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Take up thy cross, let not its weight Fill thy weak spirit with alarm;
His strength shall bear thy spirit up,
And brace thy heart and nerve thine arm.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Take up thy cross, nor heed the shame,
Nor let thy foolish pride rebel;
Thy Lord for thee the cross endured,
And saved thy soul from death and hell.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Take up thy cross then in His strength,
And calmly sin's wild deluge brave, 'Twill guide thee to a better home,
It points to glory o'er the grave.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Take up thy cross and follow Christ,
Nor think til death to lay it down;
For only those who bear the cross May hope to wear the glorious crown.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: To Thee, great Lord, the One in Three,
All praise forevermore ascend:
O grant us in our home to see
The heavenly life that knows no end.

title: That Men a godly Life Might Live (These Are the Holy Ten Commands)
author: Martin Luther

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: That man a godly life might live,
God did these ten com mandments give By His true servant Moses, high Upon the mount Sinai.
Have mercy,
Lord.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: I am thy God and Lord alone,
No other God be sides Me own;
On My great mercy venture thee,
With all thy heart love thou Me.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: By idle word and speech profane Take not My holy Name in vain;
And praise not aught as good and true But what God doth say and do.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Hallow the day which God hath blest,
That thou and all thy house may rest;
Keep hand and heart from labor free,
That God may so work in thee.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Give to thy parents hon* or due,
Be dutiful and loving too;
And help them when their strength decays So shalt thou have length of days.

title: The Advent of Our God
author: Charles Coffin

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: The advent of our God Shall be our theme for prayer Come, let us meet him on the road And place for Him prepare.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: The everlasting Son In* carnate stoops to be,
Himself the servant's form puts on To set His people free.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Come,
Zion's daughter, rise To meet your lowly King,
Nor let your faithless heart des* pise The peace He comes to bring.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: As judge, on clouds of light,
He soon will come again And all His scattered saints u* nite With Him on high to reign.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Before the dawning day Let sin be put to flight;
No longer let the law hold sway,
But walk in freedom's light.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: All glory to the Son
Who comes to set us free,
With Father, Spirit, ever One,
Through all eternity.

title: The Apostle Looked and Heard a Voice
author: Anthony Robertson

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Th'Apostle looked and heard a voice,
He saw a Lamb as had been slain;
As angels bowed and saints gave praise These words were heard in their refrain.
"There'll be no war or foe to fight,
No searing sun, no dread of night;
No more dis* tress, no more re* straint,
No more be weak, no more feel faint.
No more be weak, no more feel faint.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: They sigh no more, gone are their fears,
No cry* ing make, shed no more tears;
They grow not old, sense no more loss,
Gone are their doubts and all their dross.
There'll be no sin and no more stain,
Unknown is sick* ness, gone is pain;
The death of death, no more the hearse,
The end of grief, the end of curse.
The end of grief, the end of curse."

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: These words are spoken faith* ful* ly,
Alpha,
Omega,
Lord is He;
For all is done and done for all,
For all who come, for all who call.
Come see His face,
His hands,
His feet,
Come quench your thirst, par* take the Feast,
Come enter in while still you may,
Then Jesus bring Eternal Day.
Then Jesus bring E* ternal Day.

title: The Bridegroom Soon Will Call Us
author: Johann Walther

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: The Bridegroom soon will call us,
Come, all ye wedding guests!
May not His voice appall us,
While slumber binds our breasts;
May all our lamps be burn* ing,
And oil be found in store,
That we, with Him return* ing,
May open find the door.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: There shall we see delight* ed Our dear Redeemer's face,
Who leads our souls benight* ed To glory by His grace;
The patriarchs shall meet us,
The prophets' holy band,
Apostles, martyrs, greet us In that celestial land.

blocks.label: Verse 3
