lines: They will not blush to own us As brothers, sisters dear,
Love ever will be shown us When we with them appear;
We all shall come before Him,
Who for us Man became,
As Lord and God adore Him,
And ever bless His Name.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Our Father, rich in bless* ing,
Will give us crowns of gold And, to His bosom press* ing,
Impart a bliss untold,
Will welcome with embra* ces Of never ending love,
And deck us with His gra* ces In blissful realms above.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: In yonder home shall ne* ver Be silent music's voice;
With hearts and lips forev* er We shall in God rejoice;
The angels shall adore Him,
All saints shall sing His praise,
And bring with joy before Him Their sweetest heav'nly lays.

title: The Church's One Foundation
author: Samuel John Stone

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: The Church's one foundation Is Jesus Christ her Lord,
She is His new creation By water and the Word.
From heav'n He came and sought her To be His holy bride;
With His own blood He bought her And for her life He died.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: She is from every nation,
Yet one o'er all the earth;
Her charter of salvation,
One Lord, one faith, one birth;
One holy Name she blesses,
Partakes one holy food,
And to one hope she presses,
With every grace endued.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: The Church shall never perish!
Her dear Lord to defend,
To guide, sustain, and cherish,
Is with her to the end: Though there be those who hate her,
And false sons in her pale,
Against or foe or traitor She ever shall prevail.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Though with a scornful wonder Men see her sore oppressed,
By schisms rent asunder,
By heresies distressed: Yet saints their watch are keeping,
Their cry goes up, 'How long?' And soon the night of weeping Shall be the morn of song!

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: 'Mid toil and tribulation,
And tumult of her war,
She waits the consummation Of peace forevermore;
Till, with the vision glorious,
Her longing eyes are blest,
And the great Church victorious Shall be the Church at rest.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: Yet she on earth hath union
With God the Three in One,
And mystic sweet communion
With those whose rest is won,
With all her sons and daughters
Who, by the Master's hand
Led through the deathly waters,
Repose in Eden land.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: O happy ones and holy!
Lord, give us grace that we
Like them, the meek and lowly,
On high may dwell with Thee:
There, past the border mountains,
Where in sweet vales the Bride
With Thee by living fountains
Forever shall abide!

title: The Cloud Received Christ From Their Sight
author: Brian James Dumont

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: The cloud received Christ from their sight.
They stood, their mouths agape.
Reminded of the things He taught His people still do wait.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: The cloud kept safe God's people as Through the dry sea they trod,
And led them through the wilderness;
They truly walked with God!

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: On Sinai's height the cloud did rest To make a home below.
The Ark first then His written Word His presence now would show.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Appearing on the mercy seat within the inmost place, the Temple showed God's promises to save our fallen race.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: On mountain high Christ's face did shine like sun, a blazing light.
The cloud once more appeared on earth a truly fearful sight.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: While here in flesh You taught us, Lord
The object sure and right:
To see our Father's glory bright,
To have eternal life.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: A goal beyond our reach You've shown;
We cannot pay the price.
No work of ours atones for sin,
We cannot set things right.

blocks.label: Verse 8
lines: You are the Truth, You are the Way
for us to see His face.
You died for us a sinner's death
abandoned in our place.

blocks.label: Verse 9
lines: On Easter day, Lord, You were raised
Firstfruits of our new Life;
And in the cloud we see the day
When joy will end all strife.

blocks.label: Verse 10
lines: We wait to see the cloud's return
To be with us below,
When You fulfill Your promises
To bring us to Your home.

blocks.label: Verse 11
lines: And though we wait to see You now
We know that You are near.
Your promises to build our faith
Are stronger than our fear.

blocks.label: Verse 12
lines: You give us faith by Your strong Word
In water, wine, and bread.
The Spirit works through earthly means,
in pastures green we're fed.

title: The Comforter Has Come
author: Frank Bottome

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: O spread the tidings 'round, wherever man is found,
Wher ever human hearts and human woes abound;
Let ev'ry Christian tongue proclaim the joyful sound: The Comforter has come!
The Comforter has come,
The Comforter has come!
The Holy Ghost from

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: The long, long night is past, the morning breaks at last,
And hush'd the dreadful wail and fury of the blast,
As o'er the golden hills the day advances fast!
The Comforter has come!
heav'n,
The Father's promise giv'n;
O spread the tidings

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Lo, the great King of kings, with healing in His wings,
To ev'ry captive soul a full deliv'rance brings;
And thro' the vacant cells the song of triumph rings;
The Comforter has come!
'round,
Wherever man is found: The Comforter has come!

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: O boundless love divine!
how shall this tongue of mine To wond'ring mortals tell the matchless grace divine;
That I, a child of hell, should in His image shine!
The Comforter has come!

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Sing, till the echoes fly above the vaulted sky,
And all the saints above to all below reply,
In strains of endless love the song that ne'er will die: The Comforter has come!

title: The Day is Surely Drawing Near
author: Bartholom�us Ringwaldt

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: The day is surely drawing near,
When God's Son, the Anointed,
Shall with great majesty appear,
As Judge of all appointed.
All mirth and laughter then shall cease When flames on flames will still increase,
As Scripture truly teacheth.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: A trumpet loud shall then resound,
And all the earth be shaken;
Then all who in their graves are found Shall from their sleep awaken.
But all that live shall in that hour,
By the Almighty's boundless pow'r Be changed at His commanding.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: A book is opened then to all,
A record truly telling What each hath done, both great and small,
When he on earth was dwelling;
And every heart be clearly seen,
And all be known as they have been,
In thoughts and words and actions.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Then woe to those who scorned the Lord,
And sought but carnal pleasures,
Who here despised His precious Word,
And loved their earthly treasures!
With shame and trembling they will stand,
And at the Judge's stern command To Satan be delivered.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: O Jesus, who my debt didst pay And for my sin wast smitten Within the Book of Life, oh, may My name be also written!
I will not doubt;
I trust in Thee,
From Satan Thou hast made me free And from all condemnation.

title: The First Noel
author: English

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: The first No* el the angel did say Was to certain poor shepherds in fields as they lay;
In fields where they lay tending their sheep,
On a cold winter's night that was so deep.

blocks.label: Refrain
lines: No* el,
No* el,
No* el,
Noel,
Born is the King of Is* rael.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: They look* �d up and saw a star Shining in the east, beyond them far;
And to the earth it gave great light,
And so it continued both day and night.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: And by the light of that same star Three Wise Men came from coun* try far;
To seek for a King was their intent,
And to follow the star wherever it went.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: This star drew nigh to the northwest,
Over Beth* lehem it took its rest;
And there it did both stop and stay,
Right over the place where Je* sus lay.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Then did they know as* sur* edly With* in that house the King did lie;
One en* tered it them for to see,
And found the Babe in pov* erty.

title: The Galilean Fishers Toil (Come Blessed Jesu Come)
author: Christopher Wordsworth

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: The Galilean fishers toil all night, and nothing take;
But Jesus comes,a wondrous spoil is lifted from the lake.
Lord, when our labors are in vain and vain the help of men,
When fruitless is our care and pain,
Come blessed Jesus then!

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: The night is dark, the surges fill the bark, the wild winds roar;
But Jesus comes and all is still,the ship is at the shore.
O Lord, when storms around us howl, and all is dark and drear,
In all the tempests of the soul,
O blessed Jesus hear.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: A frail one, thrice denying Thee saw mercy in Thine eyes,
The penitent upon the tree was borne to Paradise.
In hours of sin and deep distress o show us,
Lord,
Thy Face,
In penitential loneliness,
O give us Jesus grace!

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: The faithful few retire in fear to their closed upper room;
But suddenly with joyful cheer they see their Master come.
Lord come to us, unloose our bands and bid our terrors cease,
Lift over us Thy blessed hands,
Speak, holy Jesus Peace!

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: In days, when faith will scarce be found, and wolves be in the fold,
When sin and sorrow will abound and charity wax cold,
Then hear Thy saints, who to Thee pray to bring them to their home,
Hear when the Bride and Spirit say, "Come,
Blessed Jesus,
Come!"

title: The God of Abraham Praise
author: Daniel ben Judah

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: The God of Abr'ham praise,
Who reigns enthroned above;
Ancient of everlasting days, and God of Love;
Jehovah, great I AM!
by earth and Heav'n confessed;
I bow and bless the sacred Name for* ever blessed.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: The God of Abr'ham praise, at Whose supreme command From earth I rise and seek the joys at His right hand;
I all on earth forsake, its wis* dom, fame, and pow'r;
And Him my only Portion make, my Shield and Tow'r.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: The God of Abr'ham praise,
Whose all sufficient grace Shall guide me all my happy days, in all my ways.
He calls a worm His friend,
He calls Him* self my God!
And He shall save me to the end, thro' Jesus' blood.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: He by Himself has sworn;
I on His oath depend,
I shall, on eagle wings upborne, to Heav'n ascend.
I shall behold His face;
I shall His pow'r adore,
And sing the wonders of His grace for* evermore.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Tho' nature's strength decay, and earth and hell withstand,
To Canaan's bounds I urge my way, at His command.
The wat'ry deep I pass, with Je* sus in my view;
And thro' the howling wilder* ness my way pursue.

title: The Gospel Shows The Father's Grace
author: Matthias Loy

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: The Gospel shows the Father's grace,
Who sent his Son to save our race,
Proclaims how Jesus lived and died That man might thus be justified.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: It sets the Lamb before our eyes,
Who made th'atoning sacrifice,
And calls the souls with guilt oppressed To come and find eternal rest.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: It brings the Savior's righteousness Our souls to robe in royal dress;
From all our guilt it brings release And gives the troubled conscience peace.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: It is the pow'r of God to save From sin and Satan and the grave;
It works the faith, which firmly clings To all the treasures which it brings.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: It bears to all the tidings glad And bids their hearts no more be sad;
The heavy laden souls it cheers And banishes their guilty fears.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: May we in faith its tidings learn
Nor thanklessly its blessings spurn;
May we in faith its truth confess
And praise the Lord our Righteousness!

title: The King Shall Come
author: unknown

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: The King shall come when morning dawns,
And light triumphant breaks;
When beauty gilds the eastern hills,
And life to joy awakes.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Not as of old a little child To bear, and fight, and die,
But crowned with glory like the sun That lights the morn* ing sky.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: O brighter than the rising morn When He, victorious, rose,
And left the lonesome place of death,
Despite the rage of foes.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: O brighter than that glorious morn Shall this fair morning be,
When Christ, our King, in beauty comes,
And we His face shall see.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: The King shall come when morning dawns,
And earth's dark night is past;
O haste the rising of that morn,
The day that aye shall last.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: And let the endless bliss begin,
By weary saints foretold,
When right shall triumph over wrong,
And truth shall be extolled.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: The King shall come when morning dawns,
And light and beauty brings:
Hail, Christ the Lord! Thy people pray,
Come quickly, King of kings.

title: The Law Of God Is Good And Wise
author: Matthias Loy

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: The law of God is good and wise,
And sets His will before our eyes,
Shows us the way of right eousness,
And dooms to death when we transgress.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Its light of holiness imparts The know ledge of our sinful hearts,
That we may see our lost estate And seek deliv'rance ere too late.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: To those who help in Christ have found And would in works of love abound It shows what deeds are His delight And should be done as good and right.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: When men the offered help disdain And will fully in sin remain,
Its terror in their ear resounds And keeps their wickedness in bounds.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: The law is good, but since the fall Its ho liness condemns us all;
It dooms us for our sin to die And has no pow'r to justify.

title: The Lily of the Valley (I've Found a Friend in Jesus)
author: Charles William Fry

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: I've found a friend in Jesus,
He's everything to me,
He's the fairest of ten thousand to my soul;
The Lily of the Valley, in Him alone I see All I need to cleanse and make me fully whole.
In sorrow He's my comfort,
In sorrow He's my comfort,
I'll see His blessed face,
Where rivers of delight shall ever roll.
He's the Lily

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: He all my grief has taken, and all my sorrows borne;
In temptation He's my strong and mighty tow'r;
I'll all for Him forsake now,
I'll all my idols tear From my heart for now He keeps me by His pow'r.
Though all the world forsake me, in trouble He's my stay;
He tells me every care on Him to roll.
He's the Lily in trouble He's my stay;
He tells me every care on Him to roll.
He's the Lily

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: He'll never, never leave me, nor yet forsake me here,
So I live by faith and do His blessed will;
A wall of fire about me,
I've nothing now to fear,
With His manna He my hungry soul shall fill.
When crown'd at last in glory, and Satan tempt me sore,
Through Jesus I shall safely reach the goal.
He's the Lily of the Valley, the Bright and Morning Star,
He's the fairest of ten thousand to my soul.

title: The Lord's My Shepherd
author: 1650 from the Scottish Psalter

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: The Lord's my shepherd I'll not want,
He makes me down to lie In pastures green He leadeth me The quiet waters by.
He leadeth me,
He leadeth me,
The quiet waters by,
In pastures green He leadeth me The quiet waters by.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: My soul He doth restore again,
And me to walk doth make.
Within the paths of blessedness,
E'en for His Own Name's sake;
His Own Name's sake,
His Own Name's sake,
E'en for His Own Name's sake;
Within the paths of blessedness,
E'en for His Own Name's sake.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Yea, though I walk in death's dark vale,
Yet will I fear no ill,
For Thou art with me, and Thy rod And staff me comfort still;
I'll fear no ill,
I'll fear no ill,
Yet will I fear no ill,
For Thou art with me, and Thy rod And staff me comfort still.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: My table Thou hast furnished well In presence of my foes;
My head Thou dost with oil anoint,
And my cup overflows;
It overflows,
It overflows,
And my cup overflows;
My head Thou dost with oil anoint,
And my cup overflows.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Goodness and mercy all my days Will surely follow me: And in my Father's heart always My dwelling place shall be;
My dwelling place,
My dwelling place,
My dwelling place shall be,
And in my Father's heart always My dwelling place shall be.

title: The Lord's Prayer (new)
author: Brian L. Penney

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Father in heaven,
Your name we confess,
High and exalted in bright holiness;
O may Your kingdom come,
Your will be done,
And may the earth and heav'n be joined as one.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: O Father, now our daily bread supply,
And grant forgiveness for iniquity;
May we forgive as we have been forgiv'n,
Our hearts with mercy filled, as Yours in heav'n.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: O Father, lead us from temptation's pow'r;
May we find safety from sin's trying hour;
I Lord, deliver from the evil one,
All this we ask through Your beloved Son.

title: The Love of God
author: Frederick Martin Lehman

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: The love of God is greater far Than tongue or pen can ever tell,
It goes beyond the highest star,
And reaches to the lowest hell;
The guilty pair, bowed down with care,
God gave His Son to win;
His erring child,
He reconciled,
And pardoned from his sin.
Oh love of God, how rich and pure!
How measureless and strong!

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: When hoary time shall pass away,
And earthly thrones and kingdoms fall;
When men who here refuse to pray,
On rocks and hills and mountains call;
God's love, so sure, shall still endure,
All measureless and strong;
Redeeming grace to Adam's race* The saints' and an* gels' song.
It shall forevermore endure,
The saints' and an* gels' song.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Could we with ink the ocean fill,* And were the skies of parchment made,
Were every stalk on earth a quill And every man a scribe by trade;
To write the love of God above Would drain the o* cean dry;
Nor could the scroll contain the whole,
Tho' stretched from sky to sky.

title: The Mouth of Fools Doth God Confess (Although the Fools Say with Their Mouth)
author: Martin Luther

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: The mouth of fools doth God confess,
But while their lips draw nigh Him,
Their heart is full of wickedness,
And all their deeds deny Him.
Corrupt are they, and every one Abominable works hath done;
There is not one welldo* er.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: The Lord looked down from his high tow'r On all mankind below Him,
To see if any owned His pow'r,
And truly sought to know Him;
Who all their understanding bent To search His holy Word, intent To do his will in earn* est.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: But none there was who walked with God,
For all aside had slidden,
Delusive paths of folly trod,
And followed lusts forbidden;
Not one there was who practiced good,
And yet they deemed, in haughty mood,
Their deeds must surely please Him.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: How long, by folly blindly led,
Will ye oppress the needy,
And eat my people up like bread?
So fierce are ye, and greedy!
In God they put no trust at all,
Nor will on Him in trouble call,
But be their own provi* ders.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Therefore their heart is never still,
A falling leaf dismays them;
God is with him who doth His will,
Who trusts him and obeys Him;
But ye the poor man's hope despise,
And laugh at him, e'en when he cries,
That God is his sure com* fort.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: Who shall to Israel's outcast race From Zion bring salvation?
God will himself at length show grace, And loose the captive nation;
That will he do by Christ their King; Let Jacob then be
glad and sing, And Israel be joyful.

title: The Old Rugged Cross
author: George Bennard

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: On a hill far away stood an old rugged cross,
The emblem of suff'ring and shame;
And I love that old cross where the dearest and best For a world of lost sinners was slain.
So I'll cherish the old rugged cross,
Till my trophies at last I lay down;

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: O that old rugged cross, so despised by the world,
Has a wondrous attraction for me;
For the dear Lamb of God left His glory above To bear it to dark Calvary.
I will cling to the old rugged cross,
And exchange it some day for a crown.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: In that old rugged cross, stained with blood so divine,
A won* drous beauty I see,
For 'twas on that old cross Jesus suffered and died,
To pardon and sanctify me.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: To the old rugged cross I will ever be true;
Its shame and reproach gladly bear;
Then He'll call me some day to my home far away,
Where His glory forever I'll share.

title: The People That in Darkness Sat
author: John Morison

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: The people that in darkness sat A glorious light have seen;
The light has shined on them who long In shades of death have been.
In shades of death have been.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: To hail Thee,
Sun of Righteous* ness,
The gath'ring nations come;
They joy as when the reapers bear Their harvest treasures home.
Their harvest treasures home.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: For Thou their burden dost re* move And break the tyrant's rod As in the day when Midian fell Be fore the sword of God.
Before the sword of God.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: To us a Child of hope is born,
To us a Son is giv'n,
And on His shoulder ever rests All pow'r in earth and heav'n.
All pow'r in earth and heav'n.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: His name shall be the Prince of Peace,
The Ever lasting Lord,
The Wonderful, the Counse* lor.
The God by all adored.
The God by all adored.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: His righteous government and power
Shall over all extend;
On judgment and on justice based,
His reign shall have no end.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: Lord Jesus, reign in us, we pray,
And make us Thine alone,
Who with the Father ever art
And Holy Spirit, one.

title: The Star Proclaims the King is Here
author: Coelius Sedulius

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: The star proclaims the King is here;
But,
Herod, why this senseless fear?
He takes no realms of earth away Who gives the realms of heav'n* ly day.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: The wiser Magi see from far And follow on His guiding star;
And led by light, to light they press And by their gifts their God confess.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Within the Jordan's crystal flood In meekness stands the Lamb of God And, sinless, sanctifies the wave,
Mankind from sin to cleanse and save.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: At Cana first His pow'r is shown;
His might the blushing waters own And, changing as He speaks the word,
Flow wine, obedient to their Lord.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: All glory,
Jesus, be to Thee For this Thy glad epiphany;
Whom with the Father we adore And Holy Ghost forev* ermore.

title: The Winds and Billows Loudly Roar
author: Christopher Wordsworth

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: The winds and billows loudly roar We flounder in the deep Our bark is frail, far off the shore,
And Jesus is asleep.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: "Save us, we perish,
Lord," they cry;
To Thee we fly for aid;
"A* wake!
a* wake!" they say;
but why So faithless and afraid?

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: His head is pillow'd on the stern,
As Man He is asleep;
As God He all things does dis* cern,
And endless vig* ils keep.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: He does the ele* ments con* trol;
By His Almighty Will.
The angry waves their surges roll;
And at His Word are still.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: O ye, who in the Church's Bark O'er life's rough ocean sail,
When all a* round is drear and dark, and human ef* forts fail,

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: Touch not, with rude, irreverent hands,
And coward faithlessness,
Him, who the winds and waves commands;
But wait in quietness.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: O never, never when distressed,
To doubtful means resort;
Christ's Bark, when on the billow's crest,
Is safe as in the port.

title: There's a Great Day Coming
author: Will Lamartine Thompson

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: There's a great day coming,
A great day coming,
There's a great day coming by and by;
When the saints and the sinners shall be parted right and left,
Are you ready for that day to come?
Are you ready?

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: There's a bright day coming,
A bright day coming,
There's a bright day coming by and by;
But its brightness shall only come to them that love the Lord,
Are you ready?
Are you ready for the judgment day?

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: There's a sad day coming,
A sad day coming,
There's a sad day coming by and by;
When the sinner shall hear his doom, "Depart,
I know ye not," Are you ready?
Are you ready?
For the judgment day?

title: Thine Arm, O Lord, in Days of Old (Your Hand, O Lord, in Days of Old)
author: Edward Hayes Plumptre

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Thine arm,
O Lord, in days of old, was strong to heal and save;
It triumphed o'er disease and death, o'er darkness and the grave.
To Thee they went, the blind, the dumb, the palsied and the lame,
The leper with his tainted life, the sick with fe* vered frame.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: And lo!
Thy touch brought life and health, gave speech, and strength and sight;
And youth renewed and fear relieved owned Thee, the Lord of light;
And now,
O Lord, be near to bless,
Al* mighty as of yore,
In crowded street, by restless couch, as by Gennes* aret's shore.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Be Thou our great Deliverer still,
Thou Lord of life and death;
Re* store and quicken, soothe and bless, with Thine almight* y breath.
To hands that work and eyes that see, give wisdom's heavenly lore,
That whole and sick, and weak and strong, may praise Thee ev* ermore.

title: Thou, Who at Thy First Eucharist (Lord, Who the Night You Were Betrayed or At That First Eucharist)
author: William H. Turton

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Thou, who at Thy first Eucharist didst pray That all Thy Church might be forever one,
Grant us at ev'ry Eucharist to say With longing heart and soul, "Thy will be done." O may we all one bread, one body be,
Through this blest sacrament of unity.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: For all Thy Church,
O Lord, we intercede;
Make Thou our sad di visions soon to cease;
Draw us the nearer each to each, we plead,
By drawing all to Thee,
O Prince of Peace;
Thus may we all one bread, one body be,
Through this blest sacrament of unity.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: We pray Thee too for wand'rers from Thy fold;
O bring them back, good Shepherd of the sheep,
Back to the faith which saints believed of old,
Back to the Church which still that faith doth keep;
Soon may we all one bread, one body be,
Through this blest sacrament of unity.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: So,
Lord, at length when sacraments shall cease,
May we be one with all Thy Church above,
One with Thy saints in one unbroken peace,
One with Thy saints in one unbounded love;
More bless�d still, in peace and love to be One with the Trinity in unity.

title: Though in the Midst of Life We Be
author: Martin Medieval;Luther

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Though in midst of life we be,
Snares of death surround us;
Where shall we for succor flee,
Lest our foes confound us?
To Thee alone, our Sa* vior.
We mourn our grievous sin which hath Stirr'd the fire of Thy fierce wrath.
Holy and gracious God!
Holy and mighty God!
Holy and allmerciful Sa* vior!
Let us not, we pray,
From the true faith's com* fort

blocks.label: Refrain
lines: Fall in our last need away.
Kyrie eleison.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Whilst in midst of death we be,
Hell's grim jaws o'ertake us;
Who from such dis tress will free.
Who secure will make us?
Thou only,
Lord, canst do it!
It moves Thy tender heart to see Our great sin and mis* ery.
Sa* vior!
Thou eternal God!
Save us,
Lord, from sink* ing In the deep and bitter flood.
Kyrie eleison.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Into hell's fierce agony Sin doth headlong drive us: Where shall we for succor flee,
Who,
O, who will hide us?
Thou only, blessed Sa* viour.
Thy precious blood was shed to win Peace and pardon for our sin.
Sa* vior!
Thou eternal God!
Let not hell dismay us With its deep and burning flood.
Kyrie eleison.

title: Through the Night of Doubt and Sorrow
author: Bernhardt Severin Ingemann

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Through the night of doubt and sorrow Onward goes the pilgrim band,
Singing songs of expectation,
Marching to the Promised Land.
Clear before us through the darkness Gleams and burns the guiding light: Brother clasps the hand of brother,
Stepping fearless through the night.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: One the light of God's own presence,
O'er His ransomed people shed,
Chasing far the gloom and terror,
Bright'ning all the path we tread: One the object of our journey,
One the faith which never tires,
One the earnest looking forward,
One the hope our God inspires.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: One the strain that lips of thousands Lift as from the heart of one;
One the conflict, one the peril One the march in God begun: One the gladness of rejoicing On the far eternal shore,
Where the One Almighty Father Reigns in love for evermore.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Onward, therefore, pilgrim brothers,
Onward, with the cross our aid!
Bear its shame, and fight its battle,
Till we rest beneath its shade.
Soon shall come the great awaking,
Soon the rend* ing of the tomb;
Then the scatt'ring of all shadows,
And the end of toil and gloom.

title: Tis Good, Lord, To Be Here
author: Joseph Armitage Robinson

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: 'Tis good,
Lord, to be here,
Thy glory fills the night;
Thy face and garments, like the sun,
Shine with unborrowed light.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: 'Tis good,
Lord, to be here,
Thy beauty to behold Where Moses and Elijah stand,
Thy messengers of old.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Fulfiller of the past,
Promise of things to be,
We hail Thy body glorified And our redemption see.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Before we taste of death,
We see Thy Kingdom come;
We fain would hold the vision bright And make this hill our home.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: 'Tis good,
Lord, to be here.
Yet we may not remain;
But since Thou bidst us leave the mount,
Come with us to the plain.

title: 'Tis Midnight and On Olive's Brow
author: William Bingham Tappan

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: 'Tis midnight, and on Olive's brow The star is dimmed that lately shone;
'Tis midnight, in the garden now The suff'ring Savior prays alone.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: 'Tis midnight, and from all removed Immanuel wrestles, lone, with fears;
E'en the disciple whom He loved Heeds not his Master's grief and tears.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: 'Tis midnight, from the heav'nly plains Are borne the songs that angels know;
Unheard by mortals are the strains That sweetly soothe the Savior's woe.

title: To Avert From Men God's Wrath
author: John Hus

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: To avert from men God's wrath Jesus suffered in our stead;
By an ignominious death He a full atonement made;
And by His most precious blood,
Brought us, sinners, nigh to God.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: That we never should forget This great Love on us bestowed,
He gave us His flesh to eat, and to drink His precious blood;
All who sick and needy are May receive in Him a share.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Hither each afflicted soul May repair, though filled with grief;
To the sick, not to the whole, the Physician brings relief;
Fear not, therefore, but draw nigh,
Christ will all your wants supply.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: He who in selfrighteousness Fixes any hope or stay,
Has not on a wedding dress,
And with shame is sent away;
To the hungry, weary heart,
He will food and rest impart.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: But examine first your case,
Whether you be in the faith;
Do you long for pard'ning grace?
Is your only hope His death?
Then, howe'er your soul's oppressed,
Come, you are a worthy guest.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: He who Jesus' mercy knows, Is from wrath and envy freed;
Love unto our neighbor shows That we are His flock indeed;
Thus we may in all our ways Show forth our Redeemer's praise.

title: To God Be The Glory
author: Fanny Jane Crosby

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: To God be the glory, great things He has done;
So loved He the world that He gave us His Son Who yielded His life an a tonement for sin,
And opened the life gate that all may go in.
Praise the Lord, praise the Lord,
Let the earth hear His voice!
Praise the Lord,

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: O perfect redemption, the purchase of blood,
To every believer the promise of God;
The vilest offender who truly believes,
That moment from Jesus a pardon receives.
praise the Lord,
Let the people rejoice!
O come to the Father, through

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Great things He has taught us, great things He has done,
And great our rejoicing through Jesus the Son;
But purer, and higher, and greater will be Our wonder, our transport, when Jesus we see.
Jesus the Son,
And give Him the glory, great things He has done.

title: To Jordan Came Our Lord, The Christ
author: Martin Luther

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: To Jordan came our Lord the Christ,
To do God's pleasure will* ing,
And there was by Saint John baptized,
All righteousness fulfill* ing;
There did He consecrate a bath To wash away transgres* sion,
And quench the bitterness of death By His own blood and pas* sion;
He would a new life give us.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: So hear ye all, and well perceive What God doth call bapti* sm,
And what a Christian should believe Who error shuns and schi* sm: That we should water use, the Lord Declareth it His plea* sure;
Not simple water, but the Word And Spirit without mea* sure;
He is the true Bapti* zer.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: To show us this,
He hath His Word With signs and symbols gi* ven;
On Jordan's banks was plainly heard The Father's voice from Hea* ven: "This is My wellbeloved Son,
In whom My soul delight* eth;
Hear Him." Yea, hear Him e very one Whom He Himself invi* teth,
Hear and obey His teach* ing.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: In tender manhood Jesus straight To holy Jordan wend* eth;
The Holy Ghost from Heaven's gate In dovelike shape descen* deth;
That thus the truth be not denied,
Nor should our faith e'er wa* ver,
That the Three Persons all preside,
At baptism's holy la* ver,
And dwell with the belie* ver.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Thus Jesus His disciples sent: Go teach ye every na* tion,
That lost in sin they must repent;
And flee from condemna* tion: He that be lieves and is baptized,
Obtains a mighty bless* ing;
A newborn man, no more he dies,
Eternal life posses* sing,
A joyful heir of Hea* ven.

title: To Shepherds As They Watched By Night
author: Martin Luther

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: To shepherds as they watched by night Appeared a host of angels bright;
Behold the tender Babe, they said,
In yonder lowly man* ger laid.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: At Bethlehem, in David's town,
As Micah did of old make known;
'Tis Jesus Christ, your Lord and King,
Who doth to all salva* tion bring.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Oh, then rejoice that through His Son God is with sinners now at one;
Made like yourselves of flesh and blood,
Your Brother is th'eter* nal God.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: What harm can sin and death then do?
The true God now abides with you.
Let hell and Satan rage and chafe,
Christ is your Brother ye are safe.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Not one He will or can forsake Who Him his confidence doth make.
Let all his wiles the Tempter try,
You may his utmost pow'rs defy.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: Ye shall and must at last prevail;
God's own ye are, ye cannot fail.
To God forever sing your praise
With joy and patience all your days.

title: Today Thy Mercy Calls Me (Today Your Mercy Calls Us)
author: Oswald Allen

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Today Thy mercy calls me to wash away my sin;
However great my trespass, whate'er I may have been;
However long from mercy I may have turned away,
Thy blood,
O Christ, can wash me, and make me clean today.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Today Thy gate is open, and all who enter in Shall find a Father's welcome, and pardon for their sin;
The past shall be forgotten, a present joy be given;
A future grace be promised, a glorious crown in Heav'n.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Today the Father calls me, the Holy Spirit waits,
The bless�d angels gather around the heav'nly gates;
No question will be asked me, how often I have come;
Although I oft have wandered, it is my Father's home.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: O all embracing mercy, thou ever open door,
What shall I do without thee when heart and eyes run o'er?
When all things seem against me, to drive me to despair,
I know one gate is open, one ear will hear my prayer.

title: Twas In The Moon of Wintertime (Huron Carol or Jesus He Is Born)
author: Jean de Br�beuf

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: 'Twas in the moon of wintertime,
When all the birds had fled,
That mighty Gitchi Manitou Sent angel choirs instead;
Before their light the stars grew dim,
And wand'ring hunters heard the hymn:

blocks.label: Refrain
lines: Jesus your King is born,
Jesus is born,
In excelsis gloria.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Within a lodge of broken bark The tender babe was found,
A ragged robe of rabbit skin Enwrapped His beauty 'round;
But as the hunter braves drew nigh,
The angel song rang loud and high:

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: The earliest moon of wintertime Is not so round and fair As was the ring of glory on The helpless Infant there.
The chiefs from far before Him knelt With gifts of fox and beaver pelt.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Oh children of the forest free,
Oh sons of Manitou,
The holy Child of earth and Heav'n Is born today for you.
Come kneel before the radiant Boy,
Who brings you beauty, peace and joy.

title: 'Twas On That Dark, That Doleful Night
author: Isaac Watts

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: 'Twas on that dark, that doleful night When pow'rs of earth and hell arose Against the Son of God's delight,
And friends betrayed Him to His foes:

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Before the mournful scene began,
He took the bread, and blessed, and brake: What love through all His actions ran!
What wondrous words of grace He spake!

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: "This is My body, broke for sin;
Receive and eat the living food:" Then took the cup, and blessed the wine;
"'Tis the new cov'nant in My blood."

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: For us His flesh with nails was torn,
He bore the scourge,
He felt the thorn;
And justice poured up on His head Its heavy vengeance in our stead.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: For us His vital blood was spilt,
To buy the pardon of our guilt,
When, for black crimes of biggest size,
He gave His soul a sacrifice.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: "Do this," He cried, "till time shall end,
In memory of your dying friend;
Meet at My table, and record
The love of your departed Lord."

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: Jesus, Thy feast we celebrate,
We show Thy death, we sing Thy name,
Till Thou return, and we shall eat
The marriage supper of the Lamb.

title: Under His Wings
author: William Orcutt Cushing

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Under His wings I am safely abiding,
Though the night deepens and tempests are wild,
Still I can trust Him;
I know He will keep me,
He has redeemed me, and I am His child.
Under His wings, under His wings,
Who from His love can sever?

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Under His wings, what a refuge in sorrow!
How the heart yearningly turns to His rest!
Often when earth has no balm for my healing,
There I find comfort, and there I am blessed.
Under His wings my soul shall abide,
Safely abide forever.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Under His wings, oh, what precious enjoyment!
There will I hide till life's trials are o'er;
Sheltered, protected, no evil can harm me,
Resting in Jesus,
I'm safe evermore.

title: Wake, Awake, for Night Is Flying
author: Phillipp Nicolai

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Wake, awake, for night is fly* ing;
The watchmen on the heights are crying: Awake,
Jerusalem, at last!
Midnight hears the welcome voi* ces And at the thrilling cry rejoices;
Come forth, ye virgins, night is past;
The Bridegroom comes, awake;
Your lamps with gladness take;
Alleluia!
And for His marriage feast prepare For ye must go and meet Him there.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Zion hears the watchmen sing* ing,
And all her heart with joy is springing;
She wakes, she rises from her gloom;
For her Lord comes down all glo* rious,
The strong in grace, in truth victorious.
Her Star is ris'n, her Light is come.
Ah come,
Thou blessed One,
God's own beloved Son: Alleluia!
We follow till the halls we see Where Thou hast bid us sup with Thee

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Now let all the heav'ns adore Thee,
And saints and angels sing before Thee,
With harp and cymbal's clearest tone;
Of one pearl each shining por* tal,
Where we are with the choir immortal Of angels round Thy dazzling throne;
Nor eye hath seen, nor ear hath yet attained to hear What there is ours, but we rejoice and sing to Thee Our hymn of joy eternally.

title: We All Believe in One True God (In One True God We All Believe)
author: Martin Medieval;Luther

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: We all believe in one true God,
Who created earth and heaven,
The Father, who to us in love Hath the right of children gi* ven.
He both soul and body feedeth,
All we need He doth provide us;
He through snares and perils lead* eth,
Watch* ing that no harm betide us.
He car* eth for us day and night,
All things are governed by His might.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: We all believe in Je* sus Christ,
His own Son, our Lord, possessing An equal Godhead, throne, and might,
Source of every grace and bless* ing.
Born of Mary, virgin mother,
By the power of the Spirit,
Made true man, our elder Bro* ther,
That the lost might life inherit;
Was cru* ci* fied for sin* ful men And raised by God to life again.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: We all confess the Ho* ly Ghost,
Who sweet grace and comfort giveth And with the Father and the Son In eternal glory liv* eth;
Who the Church,
His own creation,
Keeps in uni ty of spirit.
Here forgiveness and salva* tion Dai* ly come through Jesus' merit.
All flesh shall rise, and we shall be In bliss with God e* ternally.

title: We Gather Together
author: unknown

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: We gather together to ask the Lord's blessing;
He chastens and hastens His will to make known.
The wicked oppressing now cease from distressing.
Sing praises to His Name;
He forgets not His own.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Beside us to guide us, our God with us joining,
Ordaining, maintaining His kingdom divine;
So from the beginning the fight we were winning;
Thou,
Lord, were at our side, all glory be Thine!

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: We all do extol Thee,
Thou Leader triumphant,
And pray that Thou still our Defender will be.
Let Thy congregation escape tribulation;
Thy Name be ever praised!
O Lord, make us free!

title: We Give Thee But Thine Own
author: William Walsham How

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: We give Thee but Thine own,
Whate'er the gift may be;
All that we have is Thine alone,
A trust,
O Lord, from Thee.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: May we Thy bounties thus As stewards true receive,
And gladly, as Thou blessest us,
To Thee our firstfruits give.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: O hearts are bruised and dead,
And homes are bare and cold,
And lambs for whom the Shepherd bled Are straying from the fold.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: To comfort and to bless,
To find a balm for woe,
To tend the lone and fatherless Is angels' work below.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: The captive to re* lease,
To God the lost to bring,
To teach the way of life and peace?
It is a Christlike thing.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: And we believe Thy Word,
Though dim our faith may be;
Whate'er for Thine we do, O Lord,
We do it unto Thee.

title: We Know Thee Who Thou Art (Prayer After Pardon)
author: William Bright

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: We know Thee who Thou art,
Lord Jesus,
Mary's Son;
We know the yearnings of Thy heart To end Thy work begun.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: That sacred fount of grace, 'Mid all the bliss of Heav'n,
Has joy whene'er we seek Thy face,
And kneel to be forgiv'n.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Brought home from ways perverse,
At peace Thine arms within,
We pray Thee, shield us from the curse Of falling back to sin.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: We dare not ask to live Henceforth from trials free;
But oh!
when next they tempt us, give More strength to cling to Thee.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: We know Thee who Thou art,
Our own redeeming Lord;
Be Thou by will, and mind, and heart,
Accepted, loved, adored.

title: We Now Implore God the Holy Ghost
author: Martin German;Luther

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: We now implore God the Holy Ghost For the true faith, which we need the most,
That in our last moments He may befriend us And, as homeward we journey, attend us.
Lord, have mercy.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Shine in our hearts,
O most precious Light,
That we Jesus Christ may know aright,
Clinging to our Savior, whose blood hath bought us.
Who again to our homeland hath brought us.
Lord, have mercy.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Thou sacred Love, grace on us bestow,
Set our hearts with heav'nly fire aglow That with hearts u nited we love each other,
Of one mind, in peace with ev'ry bro* ther.
Lord, have mercy!

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Thou highest Comfort in ev'ry need,
Grant that neither shame nor death we heed,
That e'en then our courage may never fail us When the Foe shall accuse and assail us.
Lord, have mercy!

title: Were You There?
author: African-American

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Were you there when they crucified my Lord?
Were you there when they crucified my Lord?
Sometimes it causes me to tremble, tremble, tremble.

blocks.label: Refrain
lines: Were you there when they laid Him in the tomb?

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Were you there when they nailed Him to the tree?
Were you there when they nailed Him to the tree?
Were you there when they crucified my Lord?

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Were you there when they pierced Him in the side?
Were you there when they pierced Him in the side?
Oh!
Were you there when they nailed Him to the tree?

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Were you there when the sun refused to shine?
Were you there when the sun refused to shine?
Were you there when they pierced Him in the side?

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Were you there when they laid Him in the tomb?
Were you there when they laid Him in the tomb?
Were you there when the sun refused to shine?

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: Were you there when God raised Him from the tomb?
Were you there when God raised Him from the tomb?
Oh! Sometimes it causes me to tremble, tremble, tremble.
Were you there when God raised Him from the tomb?

title: What A Friend We Have In Jesus
author: Joseph Medlicott Scriven

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: What a Friend we have in Jesus, all our sins and griefs to bear!
What a privilege to carry everything to God in prayer!
O what peace we often forfeit,
O what needless pain we bear,
All because we do not carry everything to God in prayer.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Have we trials and temptations?
Is there trouble anywhere?
We should never be discouraged;
take it to the Lord in prayer.
Can we find a friend so faithful who will all our sorrows share?
Jesus knows our every weakness;
take it to the Lord in prayer.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Are we weak and heavy laden, cumbered with a load of care?
Precious Savior, still our refuge, take it to the Lord in prayer.
Do your friends despise, forsake you?
Take it to the Lord in prayer!
In His arms He'll take and shield you;
you will find a solace there.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Blessed Savior,
Thou hast promised Thou wilt all our burdens bear May we ever,
Lord, be bringing all to Thee in earnest prayer.
Soon in glory bright unclouded there will be no need for prayer Rapture, praise and endless worship will be our sweet portion there.

title: What Child Is This?
author: William Chatterton Dix

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: What Child is this who, laid to rest On Mary's lap is sleeping?
Whom angels greet with anthems sweet,
While shep* herds watch are keeping?
This, this is Christ the King,
Whom shepherds guard and angels sing;
Haste, haste, to bring Him laud,
The Babe, the Son of Mary.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Why lies He in such mean estate,
Where ox and ass are feeding?
Good Christians, fear, for sinners here The si* lent Word is pleading.
Nails, spear shall pierce Him through,
The cross be borne for me, for you.
Hail, hail the Word made flesh,
The Babe, the Son of Mary.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: So bring Him in* cense, gold and myrrh,
Come peasant, king to own Him;
The King of kings salvation brings,
Let lov* ing hearts enthrone Him.
Raise, raise a song on high,
The virgin sings her lullaby.
Joy, joy for Christ is born,
The Babe, the Son of Mary.

title: When I Survey the Wondrous Cross
author: Isaac Watts

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: When I survey the wondrous cross On which the Prince of Glory died,
My rich-est gain I count but loss,
And pour contempt on all my pride.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Forbid it,
Lord, that I should boast,
Save in the death of Christ my God!
All the vain things that charm me most,
I sacrifice them to His blood.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: See from His head,
His hands,
His feet,
Sorrow and love flow mingled down!
Did e'er such love and sor* row meet,
Or thorns compose so rich a crown?

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: His dying crimson, like a robe,
Spreads o'er His body on the tree;
Then I am dead to all the globe,
And all the globe is dead to me.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Were the whole realm of nature mine,
That were a present far too small;
Love so ama* zing, so di* vine,
Demands my soul, my life, my all.

title: When The Roll Is Called Up Yonder
author: James Milton Black

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: When the trumpet of the Lord shall sound, and time shall be no more,
And the morning breaks, eternal, bright and fair;
When the saved of earth shall gather over on the other shore,
And the roll is called up yonder,
I'll be there.
When the roll is called up yonder,
When the roll is called up yonder,
I'll be there,
When the roll is called up

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: On that bright and cloudless morning when the dead in Christ shall rise,
And the glory of His resurrection share;
When His chosen ones shall gather to their home beyond the skies,
When the roll is called up yonder,
I'll be there,
When the roll yonder,
When the roll is called up yonder,
I'll be there.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Let us labor for the Master from the dawn till setting sun,
Let us talk of all His wondrous love and care;
Then when all of life is over, and our work on earth is done, is called up yonder,
When the roll is called up

title: Where He Leads Me (I Can Hear My Savior Calling or Follow All The Way)
author: Edward William Blandy

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: I can hear my Savior calling,
I can hear my Savior calling,
I can hear my Savior calling, "Take thy cross and follow, follow Me." Where He leads me I will follow,
Where He leads me I will follow,

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: I'll go with Him through the garden,
I'll go with Him through the garden,
I'll go with Him through the garden,
I'll go with Him, with Him all the way.
Where He leads me I will follow;
I'll go with Him, with Him, all the way.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: I'll go with Him through the judgment,
I'll go with Him through the judgment,
I'll go with Him through the judgment,
I'll go with Him, with Him all the way.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: He will give me grace and glory,
He will give me grace and glory,
He will give me grace and glory,
And go with me, with me all the way.

title: While O'er Our Guilty Land, O Lord
author: Samuel Davies

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: While o'er our guilty land,
O Lord,
We view the terrors of Your sword,
O where can all the help* less fly?
To whom but You direct their cry?

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: On You, our guardian God, we call;
Before Your throne of grace we fall;
But is there no deliv'r* ance there?
And must we perish in despair?

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: See, we repent, we weep, we mourn;
To our forsaken God we turn;
O spare our guilty coun* try, spare The Church which You have planted there.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: We are the old, the sick, the lame;
We blind and deaf cry Jesus' Name.
We plead Your mercy for His sake,
And trust that You will not forsake.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Christ is our only righteousness,
His death for us is our redress.
Your promise stronger than our sin;
Blot out O Lord what we have been.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: We are your children after all,
Redeemed by Christ after the fall.
Marked with Your Name in Baptism,
Our home remains in Your Kingdom.

title: Whiter Than Snow
author: James L. Nicholson

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Lord Jesus,
I long to be perfectly whole;
I want Thee for- ever to live in my soul,
Break down ev'ry idol, cast out ev'ry foe;
Now wash me and I shall be whiter than snow.
Whiter than snow, yes, whiter than snow;

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Lord Jesus, look down from Thy throne in the skies,
And help me to make a complete sacrifice;
I give up myself, and what- ever I know,
Now wash me and I shall be whiter than snow.
Now wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Lord Jesus, for this I most humbly entreat,
I wait, blessed Lord, at Thy crucified feet,
By faith, for my cleansing,
I see Thy blood flow,
Now wash me and I shall be whiter than snow.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Lord Jesus,
Thou seest I patiently wait,
Come now, and with- in me a new heart create;
To those who have sought Thee,
Thou never said'st ``No,'' Now wash me and I shall be whiter than snow.

title: Wilt Thou, O Man, Live Happily (Man, Wouldst Thou Live All Blissfully)
author: Martin Luther

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Wilt thou,
O man, live happily,
And dwell with God eter* nally,
The ten commandments keep, for thus Our God Himself biddeth us.
Kyr' eleison!

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: I am the Lord and God!
take heed No other god doth thee mislead;
Thy heart shall trust alone in Me,
My kingdom then thou shalt be.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Honor My Name in word and deed,
And call on Me in time of need: Hallow the Sabbath, that I may Work in thy heart on that day.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: Obedient always, next to Me,
To father and to mo* ther be;
Kill no man: even anger dread;
Keep sacred thy marriage bed.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Steal not, nor do thy neighbor wrong By bearing wit ness with false tongue;
Thy neighbor's wife desire thou not,
Nor grudge him aught he hath got.

title: Within the Father's House
author: James Russell Woodford

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Within the Father's house The Son hath found His home;
And to His temple suddenly The Lord of Life hath come.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: The doctors of the law Gaze on the wondrous child,
And marvel at His gracious words Of wisdom undefiled.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Yet not to them is giv'n The mighty truth to know,
To lift the fleshly veil which hides Incarnate God below.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: The secret of the Lord Escapes each human eye,
And faithful pond'ring hearts await The full epiphany.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Lord, vis-it Thou our souls,
And teach us by Thy grace Each dim revealing of Thyself With loving awe to trace;

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: Till from our darkened sight
The cloud shall pass away,
And on the cleans�d soul shall burst
The everlasting day.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: Till we behold Thy face,
And know, as we are known,
Thee, Father, Son, and Holy Ghost,
Co-equal Three in One.

title: Yet Before We See Your Plans
author: Brian James Dumont

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: Yet be* fore we see Your plans,
Lord;
While the path is still unknown Bless us Lord to shout Your prai* ses,
May Your work through us be shown.
Give us faith to trust Your mercy,
Make us confident to be

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Marching round the walls of Jer'* cho Went Your trumpeted parade.
Cele* brating Your great tri* umph E'en be* fore it was displayed.
Called and holy as Your Church who Shout and sing Your victory.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: With four armies bearing on them King Je* hoshaphat would send First the band to sing your prai* ses,
Thus Your glory to extend.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: On that night before He died The Lord to You would raise a hymn He would sing Your praise and mer* cy E'en be* fore the battle grim.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: And we lowly helpless few ha* rassed and fettered by our sin More than conquerors in Christ for He did our salvation win.

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: All around us Lord we see a
World that spins and spirals down.
While our hindered human eyes can't
See You turning us around.
Give us faith to trust Your mercy,
Make us confident to be
Called and holy as Your Church who
Shout and sing Your victory.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: In our lives and times so broken
By our sin and willful pride
Or just with uncertainty, Your
Plans You often seem to hide,
Give us faith to trust Your mercy,
Make us confident to be
Called and holy as Your Church who
Shout and sing Your victory.

title: You Parents Hear What Jesus Taught
author: Ludwig Helmbold

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: You parents, hear what Jesus taught When little ones to him were brought: Forbid them not, but heed my plea Permitting them to come to me.

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Obey your Lord and let his truth Be taught your children in their youth That they in church and school may dwell And learn their Savior's praise to tell.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: For if you love them as you ought,
To Christ your children will be brought.
If thus you place them in his care,
All in your family well shall fare.

title: You People Who Now Are Baptized
author: Paul Gerhardt

blocks.label: Verse 1
lines: You people who now are baptized God's gracious love sur rounds you.
By Christ's Name you're now recognized;
Pon der what happened to you: Whose work was it which fashioned you,
Whose inborn nature that He slew,
When you first gained His promise?

blocks.label: Verse 2
lines: Before held in your mother's arm,
From your time of con ception,
Quite hostile to the Law's alarmsLet there be no deception.
A sinner born of sinner's seed;
Still God Himself for you would bleed,
He took on flesh to save you.

blocks.label: Verse 3
lines: Your soul and body turned within,
Sin filled you like a poison.
Concern for neighbor paperthin;
God's love was simply foreign.
Then raised by God the Lord of Life To glow in His eternal Light Your robe of white is gleaming.

blocks.label: Verse 4
lines: The majesty that terrifies Was all God's presence brought you.
Your fault you could not rectify;
An xiety consumed you.
A slave of sin and Satan held Trapped in a prison bound for hell Death was your only future.

blocks.label: Verse 5
lines: Then washed clean in this holy flood,
The water of Bap tism;
Instilled faith in Christ's holy blood Brought to the Father's Kingdom,
Your heart rebuilt within your breast,
New nature filled with righteousness,
Your every sin forgiven!

blocks.label: Verse 6
lines: It washes all your sins away
And makes you pure and holy.
Hell's hold on you was lost that day,
God's freedom for the lowly.
You are now truly God's dear child
An heir of heaven undefiled
With crown to cast before Him.

blocks.label: Verse 7
lines: Your nature lost in Adam's fall,
Corrupt through generations,
Refreshed now in the waterfall-
A perfect new creation!
The death of death before your eyes:
God's power must be recognized.
Hell's demons lie defeated!

blocks.label: Verse 8
lines: Now we can gladly draw to Christ
And boldly ask His blessing
Because of Jesus' sacrifice,
Our sins upon Him pressing.
The Father looks on us and sees
Christ's holiness and His good deeds:
White robes giv'n by His merit.

blocks.label: Verse 9
lines: This holy bath ... What pow'r displays!
What wondrous grace-filled cleansing;
None on their own can e'er appraise
The value of their raising.
The Word of God in simple form
Can calm the tempest and the storm.
It brings peace to your spirit.

blocks.label: Verse 10
lines: Plain water cannot wash our sin
Nor clean our inward spirit,
But water with God's promise can
Bring all the Father wills it.
The water that floods over you
From God's command has strength imbued.
His Name is placed upon you.

blocks.label: Verse 11
lines: Too precious to repay somehow,
Just grateful thanks we offer.
Christ's work has been delivered now
To you through Word and water.
Nothing but Christ's atoning work
In you could kill death's ugly smirk
You're now refreshed and holy.

blocks.label: Verse 12
lines: Now gladly live as God's dear child
Proclaim to all His Gospel
Shine to the world; be undefiled...
A beacon to all people.
Till called home to eternal joy
With new song that we'll all employ
To cast our crowns before Him.
